entries.summary: The landing pages and Compare the Tiers now show the Writing Coach, and say you can use your own art or words.
entries.detail: Both landing pages: the line under the Start buttons reads "Your own art or words, if you like"; the Arsenal strip has a fifth card, Writing Coach; Gold and Platinum list "writing coach". Compare the Tiers has a Writing Coach row (Silver: Regen only; Gold and Platinum: a tick, read from the same rule the coach uses) and a footnote: on every plan you can put your own art in the book or write it yourself. Test: open the home page and the storyteller page, wide and narrow (five cards; two with the coach across the bottom; one); open Compare the Tiers on each.

entries.summary: The Storyboard and Story tours now show the Writing Coach, and the Help assistant knows all about it.
entries.detail: The Storyboard tour has a Writing Coach step after the Narrative step, and the Narrative step no longer mentions Feedback under the box. The Story tour has a Writing Coach step after the Story box, for the Story Master. Help can now answer questions about the coach: where it is, what each tool does, Story box Feedback, plans and cost. Test: run the Storyboard tour (Narrative, then Writing Coach); run the Story tour as the Story Master (Writing Coach after Your story) and as a member (no coach step); ask Help "what does the writing coach cost?" and "what is the difference between Regen and Rewrite?".

entries.summary: The writing coach closes itself when you leave the page its box is on, and remembers where you were: press Writing Coach on the same box and your tabs are back.
entries.detail: Switch to another session tab and the coach closes; come back and press Writing Coach on the same box and its Feedback, Rewrite versions and words are still there. An answer that was still on its way lands in its tab meanwhile. Closing with × keeps them too. Moving to another session, version or campaign starts fresh. Test: Feedback on a box, switch to the Story tab (the coach closes), back to the Storyboard, Writing Coach on the same box (Feedback still there); open another session (fresh).

entries.summary: Feedback on the Story box now reads your whole story and looks at the big picture: what it is (notes, a game transcript or a written story; one chapter or the whole thing), its shape, pacing, clarity and gaps.
entries.detail: It reads the whole Story box and your Story Notes and Instructions, says what it reads as, then gives a verdict (Ready to build your book from, Close, or Needs work) with big-picture points, not line edits; transcripts are allowed to be messy. Show me is gone from the Story box; Rewrite and Word stay for working on the words. It costs one use for every 10,000 words, shown on the button. Test: a short story (1 use) and a long transcript (2+ uses on the button); the answer starts with Reads as.

entries.summary: The writing coach now knows each box's Prompt (what it should cover) and Direction (how it should be written), and you can edit both from the coach.
entries.detail: Prompt and Direction buttons sit on the coach's top line, with a tick when set; they open the same windows as the Review tab. Feedback judges whether the box covers its prompt and follows its direction (a box that misses either can't be Great) and never suggests undoing them; Show me and Rewrite stay within them. Test: set a direction on a box, then Feedback on text that ignores it (it says so); the Prompt button shows the outline Review shows.

entries.summary: Feedback now gives an honest verdict first: when your writing is truly great it says “I wouldn’t change a thing!”, when you’re close it says so with one or two small tips, and only real problems get a full list.
entries.detail: The writing coach judges each passage blind, against what a good illustrated story needs (not perfection): true to your original story, specific, in your voice, and free of stock phrases. It names what already works. The coach's Regen, Feedback, Rewrite and Word now look like tabs, so it is clear they switch views; the buttons inside each tab do the work. It no longer invents new tips after you have taken its earlier ones. Test: ask for Feedback on a rough box (Needs work, 3 to 5 tips); take its suggestions and ask again (Close or Great); a Great answer shows the green verdict and no tips.

entries.summary: Regen deletes the picture it no longer needs again, instead of leaving it in storage.
entries.detail: Since v3.2.21 every Regen past the first left the picture leaving the Revert slot in storage, because the panel's own note about that slot still named it when the clean-up ran. Now the slot and its note move on first, then the old picture is released. Pictures still used anywhere (archived, on another version, published) are kept as before. Test: Regen one panel three times; the log shows “R2 deleted: 204” after the second and third; Revert still brings back the previous picture with its style.

entries.summary: The Writing Coach now works on your Story / Session Transcript too: Feedback, Rewrite and Word, right under the story box.
entries.detail: Press Writing Coach under the Story box (Story Masters). Feedback reads up to about 6,000 words: the words you select, or the part around your cursor. Rewrite (all its choices) and Word work on the words you select, up to about 2,000 words at a time. Typing in the coach edits your story and saves it, as typing in the box does. Regen and Previous / Next stay with the Narrative boxes. Test: a long story, cursor near the end, Get feedback (tips about the end); select a paragraph, Rewrite > Clearer, Use this; reload the page and see the change kept.

entries.summary: The writing coach has tabs that keep their results, a wider panel, and the box name, Previous and Next on one line at the top.
entries.detail: Regen, Feedback, Rewrite and Word are tabs: each keeps its results while you look at the others, and clicking a tab never spends a use (each has its own start button). A tab whose results came before you edited the text says “Your text has changed since these suggestions” until you run it again. Words you select in the coach stay selected through Rewrite, and the new words are selected after Use this. Previous / Next clears the tabs, and asks first if any tab has suggestions you haven’t used. The mouse wheel over the coach scrolls only the coach. Test: Feedback, then Rewrite > Shorter on a selection, then back to Feedback (still there); edit the text (the note appears); Next with unused suggestions (asked); wheel over the coach at its end (the storyboard stays put).

entries.summary: One Writing Coach button under each Narrative box. The coach shows the box's text at the top, so you can see what you are working on wherever the box is, with every tool and Previous / Next box.
entries.detail: The row under each box is now Edit prompt, Regen, Writing Coach, Revert. The coach panel shows the box's text at the top; you can type there (it edits your story) and select words to work on just those. Below it: Regen, Feedback, Rewrite and Word, plus Revert. Rewrite's choices are Clearer, More vivid, More dramatic, Simpler, Add detail, Longer, Shorter, or your own way. Previous box and Next box move through the session without closing the coach. Results no longer repeat your text. Test: open the coach on the last box on the right of the page; type in the panel and see the box change; select a sentence, Rewrite > Shorter, Use this; Next box; Word on a selected word; Revert from the panel and from under the box.

entries.summary: Five new writing tools under every Narrative box: Rewrite, Describe, Expand, Tighten and Word. Select some words to work on just those, or use the whole box.
entries.detail: Rewrite offers Clearer, More vivid, More dramatic, Simpler, or your own instruction. Describe adds sight, sound and smell; Expand gives a rushed passage room; Tighten trims a wordy one. Each gives 3 versions to choose from, replaces only the words you selected (or the whole box), costs one writing use, and changes nothing until Use this. Word gives better choices for a selected word or short phrase and is free. Gold, Platinum and the Free Trial. Several Use this in a row: Revert goes back to before the first. The coach's uses line now reads like “Token: 1/4 used · 182 tokens left”. Test: select a sentence and press Rewrite > More vivid; Use this replaces only that sentence; select one word and press Word, click a choice, then another; Revert.

entries.summary: The Writing coach now knows your campaign's lore and the story so far, so Feedback and Regen stay true to your world and to what already happened.
entries.detail: Feedback, Show me and Regen now read the campaign's World / Lore and the previous session's Summary For Next Session, the same background Generate Narrative uses. They are told to stay consistent with both and not to retell them. Very long lore is trimmed for the coach (about 8,000 characters), so a use costs the same. Test: in a campaign with lore and a second session whose first session has a summary, press Feedback on a box that contradicts the lore (a wrong name or place) and see it pointed out; Regen a box and see it fit what came before.

entries.summary: Fantasy pastel is now Soft pastels, and Fantasy oil is now Oil painting. They are mediums, so they suit any kind of story.
entries.detail: New names on the art style cards, in the Library's art style filter, on Bookshelf books and in picture alt text. Nothing else changes: books and pictures already made in these styles keep them, and the pictures are drawn exactly as before. Test: open the art style picker (Soft pastels and Oil painting, same pictures and descriptions); a campaign already set to either style shows the new name; the Library art style filter lists the new names and still finds the old pictures.

entries.summary: The tour's "Whose version?" step now points at the version picker instead of a spot beside it.
entries.detail: Since the version picker was redrawn with pins, the real dropdown underneath is hidden as a 1-pixel box, and the tour was outlining that box (next to the New Version button). Both version steps (session and Publish) now point at the picker you see, falling back to the old one if it is not drawn yet. The Storyboard tour's Replace step now also says you can replace a picture with your own. Test: run the session tour; step 4 outlines the version picker. Run the Publish tour; Whose version? outlines its picker. The Storyboard tour's Replace step mentions your own image.

entries.summary: You now need to be 18 or older to open a Campaignia account. Children are still welcome in the stories you make.
entries.detail: Sign-up, the server check, Terms of Service §2 and the Privacy Policy's children section now say 18 (or the age of majority where you live, if older), in line with the terms of the AI services that draw the pictures. Existing accounts are unchanged. Terms and Privacy are now Version 1.2, October 21, 2026. Test: sign up with a date of birth 17 years ago (refused, message says 18) and 18 years ago (allowed); read Terms §2 and Privacy §12.

entries.summary: The picture model can now be switched with two Railway variables.
entries.detail: FAL_IMAGE_MODEL and FAL_IMAGE_EDIT_MODEL (unset = Nano Banana 2, as before). For Nano Banana 2.1 set google/nano-banana-2.1 and google/nano-banana-2.1/edit, and NANO_THINKING_LEVEL=minimal. A side-by-side of all 11 styles showed the same look and speed at about half the cost per picture. A value that is not a fal endpoint path is ignored. Test: set the three on staging, generate a panel, a reference, a retouch and a title; unset to go back.

entries.summary: Narrative boxes are tidier: Edit prompt, Feedback and Regen sit on one small row under the text, and the empty direction line is gone.
entries.detail: The writing pills moved from above the box to the row under it, beside Edit prompt, all the same small size. With no direction set, the 'No direction set' line is hidden (it appears again as soon as a direction is set). Undo after Use this is now called Revert, like on pictures. The uses line in the Writing coach is in smaller print. Test: Storyboard narrative box with and without a direction; Use this then Revert.

entries.summary: The Regenerate pill on pictures is now ↻ Regen, the same as on narrative boxes.
entries.detail: Storyboard panels, character reference pictures and asset pictures. Shorter, so the pill row is less likely to wrap. The tours and the prompt editor's note say Regen too. Test: a storyboard panel's pill row; a character and an asset picture.

entries.summary: Writing coach: press Feedback above any Narrative box for 3 to 5 tips that make it stronger, each with a Show me.
entries.detail: New pill row above every Narrative box you can edit on the Storyboard. Feedback (Gold, Platinum and the Free Trial; members follow the Story Master's plan) reads that one box with its neighbours and the campaign's characters, genre, voice and Story Instructions, and returns 3 to 5 suggestions with a why. Show me rewrites just that part, before and after, with Use this and Copy. Uses: 1 token buys 4 uses; Feedback and each Show me are one use; a use is taken only after the answer arrives. Below Gold the pill shows a Gold tag and explains the plans. Test: Gold account, Feedback on a panel; Show me; Use this then Undo; uses count down 4 per token; Silver sees the Gold tag.

entries.summary: Regen on a Narrative box now rewrites only that box, shows you the new text first, and costs one writing use.
entries.detail: Regen used to run the whole Generate Narrative job: it saved new text into every box and the Summary for Next Session and charged a full narrative, though only the clicked box changed on screen (TD-998). Now it writes that box alone in the same voice, length, narrator and steering, shows it in the Writing coach with Use this, Copy and Try again, and saves nothing until Use this. Every plan keeps Regen. Generate Narrative is unchanged. Test: Regen one box, reload without pressing Use this (nothing changed); Use this, reload (only that box changed, Summary untouched); one use charged.

entries.summary: The Pen and ink style card now describes its sepia washes, and the app spells color the American way.
entries.detail: Pen and ink card: 'Fine pen-and-ink linework and crosshatching with warm sepia washes, fading out to a clean white edge.' (it is not black and white only). Customer-facing text changed from colour to color: the Anime and Pastel cards, title color notes and tooltip, the print color messages, the cover tour step, the custom style builder's question labels and hints, and the help assistant's guide. Image prompts are unchanged. Test: Art Style window cards; custom style builder shows Color; ask help about title color.

entries.summary: Shorter Dark Fantasy description in the Art Style window.
entries.detail: The Dark Fantasy card no longer ends with 'and it takes its time of day from your scene' (Ian: it is implied). Card text only; the style itself is unchanged. Test: open the Art Style window and read the Dark fantasy card.

entries.summary: Seven art styles were refreshed. Pastel has a new, softer chalk look, and Charcoal and Pen and ink now fade cleanly to a white edge.
entries.detail: Dark and gritty, Fantasy oil, Cel-shaded, Watercolor, Pastel, Charcoal and Pen and ink describe their look in their own words instead of naming artists or games (TD-997). Each was tested on the group scene and keeps its character; Pastel was reworked into a paler, powdery, chalkier style. The seven style card pictures were redrawn to match. Existing pictures do not change until regenerated. The old wording is kept so a book can be finished in its original look with a custom style. Test: open the Art Style window (seven new pictures) and regenerate one panel in Pastel.

entries.summary: Character cards and your custom art style cards now show a big picture across the top instead of a small circle.
entries.detail: Characters show their whole figure in a tall picture at the top of the card (click to enlarge); custom style cards show a wide picture (the chosen Group preview, else the first reference). Edit and Delete sit on the picture. Test: open Characters and Custom Art Styles on a laptop and a phone; drag a picture onto a character card to replace its portrait.

entries.summary: Every included art style now shows a sample picture in the Art Style window, so you can see each look before you choose it.
entries.detail: The eleven included style cards carry a picture strip like the custom cards: the same group scene in every style (Everyday life and Anime in a modern cafe). Custom style cards now show the chosen description's Group preview when one was made, otherwise the first reference picture as before. Test: open the Art Style window; every included card has a picture; a custom style with a chosen winner and a Group preview shows that preview.

entries.summary: Anime has a new look: big sparkling eyes on every character, soft painted shading and glowing, dreamy light.
entries.detail: The Anime art style was rewritten from Ian's examples and tested over a dozen runs. It is no longer treated as a comic style, so it paints rather than inks. Existing pictures do not change until regenerated. Test: regenerate a close panel and a group panel in Anime; every face, including older characters, should have large anime eyes.

entries.summary: Watercolor pictures now fade out to a clean white edge, as the style always promised.
entries.detail: Watercolor joined the soft-edge styles and its description gained the edge sentence Ian tested. Existing Watercolor pictures stay full bleed until regenerated. Test: regenerate any panel in Watercolor; the paint should thin out to white before the edges.

entries.summary: Dark Fantasy now paints a grounded, realistic world with dramatic light at any time of day, instead of turning every scene into night.
entries.detail: The Dark Fantasy art style was rewritten (Ian's tested 'Grounded 2' wording). It now takes the time of day from the scene: a scene that does not name its hour should come out as day, not sunset or night, and a scene that says midday should look like midday. Indoors and underground it stays moody, with any fire, torch or lamp glowing warm. Test: regenerate an outdoor daytime panel and an indoor torchlit panel in Dark Fantasy; neither should look like night unless the scene is set at night. Existing pictures do not change until regenerated. The card in the Art Style window has a new description.

entries.summary: A panel's art style label now updates as soon as you regenerate it in a different style, and Revert brings back the old label with the old picture.
entries.detail: On the Storyboard, the line under each panel (style, type, shape) kept the style the picture had before a Regenerate until the page was reloaded, e.g. Self Illustrated after an uploaded picture was regenerated in a custom style. It now changes when the new picture lands. Revert after a Regenerate also puts back the previous picture's style label. Test: upload a picture onto a panel, Regenerate it in another style (label changes without a reload), then Revert (label goes back).

entries.summary: The note under the Title and Subtitle boxes goes away once you draw the title again with the new words.
entries.detail: After changing the subtitle and using a freshly drawn title, the note saying the drawn title still shows the old words stayed on screen until the page was reloaded. It now updates as soon as the Title Builder closes.

entries.summary: Books shelved before v3.2.10 keep the subtitle they were shelved with.
entries.detail: v3.2.18 gave old shelf books the subtitle from their version's drawn title as it is now, so a series shelved from one version (Book I, II, III) all showed the latest book's subtitle. An old book's cover was never recorded, so its subtitle is no longer changed.

entries.summary: Books on the Bookshelf show the subtitle that is on their cover, now also in small text on the spine.
entries.detail: When a book's cover uses a title drawn with the Title Builder, its subtitle is part of the drawing, so the open book on the shelf now shows that subtitle rather than whatever is in the Subtitle box. Books already on the shelf are corrected the next time the shelf opens. The spine of a book with a subtitle shows it as a second, smaller line beside the title.

entries.summary: Pictures made with AI tools are no longer flagged as naming a creator or copyright holder.
entries.detail: Image tools such as Google's write a credit like “Made with Google AI” into every picture they make, and the rights check read that as an owner — so even a title drawn with the Title Builder was flagged when used as a reference. AI tool credits no longer count, and warnings already given for that reason alone are cleared. A real name in a picture's details still warns, and stock-library pictures are still refused.

entries.summary: A loaded book is ready to publish at once, the Bookshelf shows a book's saved subtitle, and a note says when a drawn title no longer matches the Title and Subtitle boxes.
entries.detail: The Publish card no longer says “nothing yet — run Optimize first” while a book is loaded. A book put on the Bookshelf shows the subtitle it was saved with. If your cover uses a title drawn with the Title Builder and you change the Title or Subtitle, a short note under the boxes says the drawing still shows the old words.

entries.summary: Opening a campaign's book now starts on Sessions, or on Optimize when your last optimized book was never published or ordered.
entries.detail: A first book and the next book in a series both start by choosing sessions, so that is where you land. If you optimized a book and left before publishing or ordering it, you land on Optimize instead, where Load Last Optimized brings it back. Within the same visit you return to the tab you were on, with your book still loaded. Reorder still goes straight to Order & Publish.

entries.summary: A Story Master publishing his own named version no longer puts sessions unticked in that version into the online book, and the title note on publishing says it means the printed cover.
entries.detail: For a book saved before v3.2.12, the online reading page was built from the Canonical's Include in Print ticks rather than the named version's, so a session unticked in the version still appeared. It now follows the version on screen. When the printed cover and the Library listing carry different titles, the note now reads “The printed cover of this book reads …, but the Library listing and the online book say …”.

entries.summary: Drawn chapter titles in an optimized Picture Book are drawn like Prep & Preview: small, centred, transparent and unframed.
entries.detail: A session title made with the title builder used to come out full width, framed and as tall as a picture in the optimized Picture Book. It now takes half the column with no frame or caption, as it does in Prep & Preview, so those books can come out a little shorter. Run Optimize again to update a saved book.

entries.summary: A published story's online reading page now shows the saved book you published, not today's sessions and settings.
entries.detail: Optimize and save a book, then change it (untick a session, edit a scene, change the subtitle) and publish the saved book: the Library page reads exactly like the saved PDF. The same is true of a book brought back from the Bookshelf. Books saved before this version publish as they did before. The Publishing line on the Optimize tab names the loaded book's own title, and the Optimize page count now reads like “18 pages including covers”.

entries.summary: Order & Publish now shows only a book you put there: one you have just optimized, or one you load with Load Last Optimized. It says which book is loaded, and warns only if you change the book after that.
entries.detail: Open a campaign and go straight to Order & Publish: nothing is loaded, and a Load Last Optimized button sits at the top with when that book was saved. Press it: a Loaded line names the save time, the sessions, the title and the layout, and the order form and Publish appear. Optimize and save a book: it is loaded at once. Change a session tick, the layout or the cover afterwards: “You’ve changed this book since it was optimized” names what changed. Load an older book: no warning about how it differs from today. Leave the campaign or reload: nothing is loaded again. Reorder from My Orders is unchanged. The page count now reads like “16 interior pages”, and the Optimize tab's Sessions included count follows an Include in Print change straight away.

entries.summary: A printed or published book now always carries the cover, title and subtitle it was optimized with, and the “Sessions don’t match” warning no longer appears by mistake on your own named versions.
entries.detail: Optimize and save a book, then change its cover picture, title or subtitle without optimizing again. Order: the cover preview shows the SAVED cover and title, matching the book's own first page. Publish: the Library card's picture and title are the saved book's. Bookshelf: save, change the cover, Bring back, order: the shelved cover. As Story Master on one of your own named versions whose Include in Print ticks differ from the Canonical's: Optimize, save, open Order & Publish: no “Sessions don’t match”. Books saved before this version keep using the current cover settings.

entries.summary: A book with no cover chosen now uses the campaign's current picture everywhere: the preview, the printed cover and the published book show the same picture as the Cover tile.
entries.detail: On a campaign whose campaign image was changed after Prep & Preview was first opened, and whose book has no Cover chosen: the Cover tile, Refresh preview, the Order tab's cover and Publish all show the CURRENT campaign image. Before, the tile showed the new picture and the preview drew the old one (or nothing) until the Cover was removed and added again. A chosen Cover and a removed Cover are unchanged; a campaign with no campaign image still has a blank cover. Saving a book to the Bookshelf uses the same picture.

entries.summary: Campaign and session books now show their picture from the top of the book down to the title, whatever its shape, and a campaign with no picture chosen shows the opening picture of its first session.
entries.detail: My Campaigns, a campaign's Sessions page and Order & Publish → Sessions: every picture fills the book from just under the gold line to just above its own words, with the fade under the gold line; a wide or tall picture is trimmed from its middle. A drawn chapter title (Title Builder) is never trimmed: it fits whole. A campaign with no campaign image shows the opening picture of the first session in your pinned version (or your first version), else the Canonical's; choosing a campaign image replaces it. The session list shows each session's picture from your pinned version, falling back to the Canonical's when your version has none. Order & Publish still shows the version picked at the top. A watermarked (rejected) picture is never used. The printed book cover is unchanged.

entries.summary: The email-change emails come from noreply again; the warning still tells you to email support@campaignia.com.
entries.detail: Start an email change on My Account. Both emails show From: Campaignia <noreply@campaignia.com> (the FROM_EMAIL setting), not support. The warning's last line still reads “If you can't sign in, email us at support@campaignia.com and we'll help.” with the address as a link, and Reply still addresses support@campaignia.com.

entries.summary: The emails about changing your account email now come from support@campaignia.com, and the warning to your old address tells you to write to support@campaignia.com if you can't sign in.
entries.detail: Start an email change on My Account. Both emails (“Confirm your new Campaignia email” to the new address and “Your Campaignia email is being changed” to the old one) show From: Campaignia <support@campaignia.com>. The warning's last line reads “If you can't sign in, email us at support@campaignia.com and we'll help.” with the address as a link, and pressing Reply addresses support@campaignia.com. Every other Campaignia email is unchanged.

entries.summary: Opening an email-change link that has already been used or cancelled now tells you your email was not changed, instead of opening Campaignia with no message.
entries.detail: Start an email change on My Account, press Cancel change, then open the link from the confirmation email while signed in: a Campaignia window says “Email not changed” and why. Do the same with a link you have already used. Then do a real change and click its link: “Your email address has been changed.” appears, whichever address (with or without www) the link opens on. Signed out, the same results show on the sign-in page.

entries.summary: Changing your email on My Account now sends a confirmation link to the new address, and your account keeps its current email until you click it. Email addresses are no longer case-sensitive, so you can sign in however you type the capitals.
entries.detail: On My Account, type a new address in the email box: a Current password box appears. Fill it in and press Save profile. The new address gets “Confirm your new Campaignia email” (link good for 24 hours) and the old address gets “Your Campaignia email is being changed”. Until the link is clicked, sign-in and receipts keep using the old address, and My Account shows “Waiting for confirmation” with Resend link and Cancel change. Click the link: you land back in Campaignia with “Your email address has been changed” (or on the sign-in page if that browser is not signed in). Also try: a wrong password (refused, nothing sent), an address another account already uses (refused), the same address in different capitals (it is already yours), Cancel change then the old link (not valid any more), and signing in with your email typed in capitals (works). While viewing as a customer, the email change is refused.

entries.summary: Pressing Back on your campaigns list now asks “Leave Campaignia?” in Campaignia’s own window instead of the browser’s.
entries.detail: On the campaigns list (the first page after you sign in), press the browser or phone Back button. A Campaignia window asks “Leave Campaignia?” (in the installed app: “Return to the Campaignia home screen?”) with Stay and Leave. Stay keeps you on the campaigns list, and Back asks again. Leave takes you to the page you came from, or to the Campaignia home page if the app was the first page in that tab. Pressing Back again while the window is open keeps you in the app with just the one window showing.

entries.summary: You can now replace a story you have already published with a new version. It keeps its link, its place in the Library and its Bookshelf entries, so links you have shared keep working.
entries.detail: Fix what you want, run Optimize, then go to Order & Publish. If you have already published from this campaign, choose which story to replace under Publish as, then press Publish to Library and confirm. The pages, cover, title and blurb become the new version; the old version is gone. Removing a story from Published Stories now asks in Campaignia’s own window and says that links you have shared will stop working.

entries.summary: In the custom art style builder, the message at the top about a refused reference picture now goes away as soon as you replace that picture.
entries.detail: Put a watermarked picture in a reference box and press Analyze: the box goes red and a message appears at the top. Replace the picture: the red box, the note under it and the message at the top all clear.

entries.summary: Deleting a custom art style now asks in Campaignia’s own window instead of the browser’s. Removing a Library story from your Bookshelf no longer says the story stays in the Library when it has already left.
entries.detail: Open Custom Art Styles and press Delete on a style: a Campaignia window asks “Delete this custom style?” with Delete and Keep it; Keep it changes nothing, Delete removes it. On the Bookshelf, remove a Library book whose story is still published: the note says it stays in the Library. Remove one whose story was taken out of the Library: the note says it is no longer in the Library.

entries.summary: Analyze in the custom art style builder now refuses a watermarked reference picture in a few seconds instead of after the whole analysis, names it by its slot (Reference 1, Reference 2 and so on), and outlines that reference box in red with the reason until the picture is replaced. A signed reference gets an amber note and Analyze carries on.
entries.detail: In Custom Art Styles, start a new style, put a picture with a watermark in Reference 1 and a clean one in Reference 2, and press Analyze: within a few seconds a red note by the button says “Reference 1: This picture has a watermark… Nothing was charged.”, the Reference 1 box is outlined red with the reason under it, and the token balance does not move. Replace the picture in Reference 1: the red outline and note go. Put a signed picture in a slot instead: it gets an amber note and the analysis runs as normal. Each picture is looked at once, so pressing Analyze again does not look again.

entries.summary: The Title Builder now looks at your reference picture when you press Generate. One with a watermark (a stock library mark, a web address or social handle stamped on it, a copyright notice) is refused before anything is drawn or charged, and is marked red in its slot; a signed one is marked amber and still used. The lettering you want copied is never mistaken for a watermark.
entries.detail: Open the Title Builder, add a reference picture with a watermark across it and press Generate: a red note by the button says it can’t be used and nothing was charged, the token balance does not move, and the picture in the slot is outlined red. Use clean decorative lettering instead: Generate draws the title as before. The same picture is looked at only once, so pressing Generate again costs nothing extra. Test pictures: 08 (clean lettering, should pass), 09 (lettering with a stock watermark, should be refused), 10 (lettering with a web address in a corner, should be refused) in the rights-test folder.

entries.summary: A picture rejected for a watermark or as a stock photo can no longer be retouched: Retouch on an asset, a story panel, a character’s reference picture or a drawn title says why by the button and charges nothing. A retouched picture also keeps the rejection of the picture it was made from, so an edit can never clear the red mark.
entries.detail: On a red (rejected) asset, press Edit, then Retouch, type a change and press Retouch image: a red note by the button says it can’t be retouched and nothing was charged; the token balance does not move. The same on a red story panel (Retouch on the Storyboard), on a character’s reference picture and in the Title Builder. Regenerate still works on an asset with a description: it draws a fresh picture from the words, not from the rejected picture. Signed (amber) pictures can be retouched as before.

entries.summary: Asking help how to write a book yourself now gets all three ways, leading with Outline / I’ll write it: write over bullet points while Campaignia draws, keep a story you have already written word for word, or draw the pictures too. The empty Archives page no longer mentions a treasure-chest button that isn’t there; it says to press Archive on a picture.
entries.detail: Ask the help assistant “I want to write a book where I do the writing. What is the best way to approach this in Campaignia?”. The answer names Outline / I’ll write it first, then Already Written for a story that is finished, and I’ll illustrate it myself only for drawing the pictures too; if it is unclear, it asks whether the story is already written. Open the Archives page of a campaign with nothing archived: it reads “Nothing archived yet. Press Archive on any picture (a panel, a character’s reference picture or a drawn title) to save a copy here.”

entries.summary: A picture rejected for a watermark or as a stock photo can no longer be archived, or chosen from the Archive as a cover, campaign picture, title or replacement. A published story never uses one as its cover: publishing picks the first clean picture, and a story page, the Library, your Published Stories and your Bookshelf show a plain box instead of one already there. Link previews leave it out.
entries.detail: Press Archive on a rejected (red) panel or character picture: a red note by the button says it can’t be archived, and nothing is added. A rejected picture already in the Archive shows red there; choosing it as the front or back cover, the campaign picture, a panel or character replacement, an asset or a title is refused the same way. Put a rejected picture on the first panel of a book with no campaign cover and publish: the story’s cover is the next clean picture. A story published earlier with a rejected cover shows the grey Picture removed box on its page, in the Library, on Published Stories and on the Bookshelf, and its link preview has no picture. Signed (amber) pictures are unaffected.

entries.summary: The Title Builder, the character window and the campaign details window (new campaign and editing) now have a ?s button, like the Custom Art Style builder and Retouch: a few tips for that window, then ask us anything about it.
entries.detail: Open each window and press ?s at the top right: the help box opens over the window with tips for it at the top (Title Builder: the words come from the book, describe the lettering, a reference picture, a token per Generate; character: nicknames after a slash, looks and personality, more reference pictures, then Build; campaign: Lore, up to three genres, the Campaign Prompt, set up characters first). Ask a question there: the answer is about that window without being told which one. Pressing ?s again does not repeat the tips.

entries.summary: When building a character leaves out a rejected picture, the message now stays under the Build button until the next build, as well as showing beside it. A picture that looks signed, or whose file details name a creator, now has a written amber note under it, not only an amber outline, so it can be read on a phone.
entries.detail: Give a character a watermarked portrait and a clean full body picture, then press Build. The note by the button says one picture was left out, and the same sentence stays in the line under the button after the note goes and after the reference picture arrives. Press Build again: the line clears and is written again. Put a signed picture (or one whose file details name an artist) in a slot or in the asset library: an amber note under it says what was found and to use it only if it is yours or you have permission. Replace it: the note goes.

entries.summary: Character pictures are checked for watermarks as soon as they are saved, not only when the character is built. Building a character now leaves out any rejected picture and uses the others; it stops only when every picture is rejected. Whenever something is refused over a picture, a red note appears next to the button you pressed.
entries.detail: Upload a watermarked picture into a character slot and save: it is outlined in red with a red note under it straight away, and the Company page shows the Picture removed box for it. Add a clean picture to another slot and press Build: the character is built from the clean picture, and a note by the button says one picture was left out. With only the watermarked picture, Build stops with a red note by the button every time it is pressed, and nothing is charged. Replace the picture: the red outline and note go at once, as does an amber (signed) outline. The small icons on the reference picture slots are gone.

entries.summary: A picture rejected for a watermark or as a stock photo is never drawn in a book: the preview, the PDF, the print files and the public story page show a plain “Picture removed” box in its place until you replace it. It also no longer shows on the Library picture wall.
entries.detail: Put a watermarked picture on a panel with Upload your own (it is marked red on the Storyboard). Open Prep and Preview: that panel shows a grey “Picture removed – watermark or stock picture” box. Download the PDF: the same box. Replace the picture with a clean one: the preview shows the new picture. A rejected picture used as a front or back cover shows the box on the cover too. A rejected picture that was made public in the Library no longer appears on the picture wall. Warned (signed) pictures are drawn as normal.

entries.summary: Character pictures and custom style samples are now checked for watermarks and signatures when they are analysed. A watermarked picture stops the character build or the style analysis, with nothing charged, until it is replaced.
entries.detail: Give a character a clearly watermarked picture (a stock preview with its logo across it) and press Build: it stops, says which picture, charges nothing, and the picture is marked red until replaced. A signed picture builds as normal with an amber reminder. Analyze a custom style with a watermarked sample: refused, names the sample, nothing charged. With a rejected uploaded picture and no reference image yet, Re-roll, Retouch, Restyle and amending a character in a session are refused too.

entries.summary: Uploaded pictures are now checked for watermarks and stock-photo labels. A watermarked or stock picture is marked in red and left out of generations until you replace it; a signed picture gets a reminder to use only art you have the rights to.
entries.detail: Upload an asset or Upload your own onto a panel with a clearly watermarked picture (for example a stock photo preview with its logo across it): a red box says it cannot be used, and the picture shows a red outline and a red note until it is replaced; the asset is no longer used as a reference in new pictures. Upload a picture with an artist signature in a corner: an amber reminder, and the picture is used as normal. Upload a stock photo whose file details name Getty, Shutterstock, iStock or similar, as a character picture, an asset, a panel picture or a custom style sample: refused or marked the same way. A plain photo or drawing: nothing is said. The check costs no tokens.

entries.summary: Behind the scenes: every picture on a public story page and in the Library picture wall now carries a short description of what it shows, for search engines and screen readers. Nothing on screen changes.
entries.detail: Open a published story, right-click a panel picture and Inspect: its alt text is the panel scene description, then its art style and genre (for example: Two adventurers climb a ruined tower. Dark Fantasy illustration, Fantasy). Stories published before this version have it too. A custom style reads just illustration. On the Library picture wall, Inspect a picture: same kind of label. The printed book and the Download PDF are unchanged.

entries.summary: On a phone, closing the Install Campaignia banner now keeps it closed, and it stops appearing once the app is installed.
entries.detail: On an Android phone in a browser tab: wait for the Install banner, press x, close the tab and come back the next day: no banner. Install the app from the banner, then open the site in that same browser: no banner. Open the installed app once, then the site in the same browser: no banner. The Install app item in the profile menu still appears whenever the browser offers an install. A different browser on the same phone cannot see an install made by another browser, so it may show the banner once until x is pressed.

entries.summary: Support sessions (Viewing as) now end after 30 minutes idle rather than 30 minutes from the start, warn in the last five minutes with a Stay button, and say so when they end.
entries.detail: Start a support session and keep working (clicking, scrolling, reading a book in preview) for more than 30 minutes: it stays open. Leave it untouched: about 25 minutes later the banner counts down with a Stay button; Stay resets it to 30 minutes. Leave it to run out: a notice says the session ended after 30 minutes idle, and OK reloads the page as yourself. Reload during a session: the clock starts again. Leave a support tab in the background for over 30 minutes: it ends (background checks do not count as activity). The Dashboard support log still records the end as expiry.

entries.summary: Going back to a session no longer leaves another page, such as Custom Art Styles, showing underneath the Storyboard.
entries.detail: Open a session, open Custom Art Styles from the profile menu, press Back: only the session shows, nothing below the Storyboard. Same with the browser back button. Also open My Stuff, Account or the Asset Library and then open a session from a link or the session arrows: nothing from the earlier page stays underneath.

entries.summary: The Custom Art Styles page has a Back button, like the Archive, Asset Library and My Stuff pages.
entries.detail: Open Custom Art Styles from the profile menu while on My Campaigns, on your Account, inside a campaign (Characters, say) and inside a session: Back returns to each of those. Reload the page while on Custom Art Styles, then Back: it goes to My Campaigns. Inside a campaign, the campaign menu on the left comes back too.

entries.summary: Behind the scenes: Campaignia can now serve pictures from its own address (images.campaignia.com) while every existing picture keeps working. Nothing changes until it is switched on.
entries.detail: On its own this release changes nothing: every picture, upload, retouch, archive, publish and order should behave exactly as before. After Ian switches staging (R2_LEGACY_PUBLIC_URLS = the old r2.dev address, R2_PUBLIC_URL = https://images.campaignia.com): new pictures are stored under images.campaignia.com; old panels still show and still work in Retouch and anything that reads a picture; archive, restore and delete work on old and new pictures; a public story page and the Library show their pictures under images.campaignia.com; a sandbox print order passes the printer file check and Lulu accepts the files. Spec claude/IMAGE_DOMAIN_SPEC.md.

entries.summary: The storyteller landing page (/story) may now appear in search results, and it is listed in the sitemap.
entries.detail: View the source of /story: no robots noindex line. Open /sitemap-pages.xml: it lists /story after /our-story. Staging still keeps every page out of search, so the real check is on production after the promote: Search Console and Bing URL Inspection on campaignia.com/story should say indexing is allowed.

entries.summary: The Library page heading is now a real page heading for search engines; it looks exactly the same.
entries.detail: Open /library on a computer and on a phone: The Public Library heading looks and sits exactly as before. View source: it is an h1. Once on production, Bing URL Inspection on /library should no longer report H1 tag missing.

entries.summary: Search engines are told not to list the signed-in app, the login page, invitation links or password reset.
entries.detail: Staging already tells search engines to stay away from every page, so this shows on production. After the promote, in the browser developer tools (Network tab, the page request), open campaignia.com/login, /app.html, /reset-password and an invite link: each response carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex. The home page, Library, Our Story and a public story page must NOT carry it.

entries.summary: The admin-only DRAFT link is no longer in the home page for every visitor; it is added only when an admin is signed in.
entries.detail: Signed out, view the home page source: no DRAFT and no link to /story. Signed in as an admin, the home page menu shows DRAFT before SIGN IN and it opens the storyteller page. Signed in as anyone else: no DRAFT.

entries.summary: The style builder's ?s now works like Retouch's: a few tips, then ask anything. The ready-made questions are gone, and help knows you are in the builder.
entries.detail: Open the style builder and click ?s: the tips appear, then the box to ask; no common questions. Ask something about detail or colour: the answer is about your custom style, without asking whether you mean a built-in one.

entries.summary: The Convert to questions button is gone from the custom art style builder; an older style is brought onto the questions with Analyze style.
entries.detail: Open a style made before the questions: no Convert button; the note says to click Analyze style. Analyze it: the answers and three descriptions appear, and the style keeps drawing as before until you pick a winner and save. Ask the help assistant about older styles: it should say Analyze, not Convert.

entries.summary: The custom art style builder has its own ?s help button, with a few tips and six ready-made questions you can click.
entries.detail: Open the style builder and click ?s beside the x. Help opens over the builder with tips for custom styles and six common questions above the box you type in. Click one: it is asked and answered as if typed, and the questions stay for another. Close help and open it from the main ?s: no questions shown.

entries.summary: Replace and Remove under each reference image in the style builder now line up.
entries.detail: Open the style builder with reference pictures in place: Replace and Remove under each one are the same height, tops level.

entries.summary: The help assistant now says a custom art style appears under the name you gave it, in My Custom Styles, and explains the close question.
entries.detail: Ask the help assistant: How do custom art styles work? Where does my custom style show up? It should say: by the name you gave it, under My Custom Styles in the Art style window (never as High fantasy illustration). Ask: What happens if I close the style builder without saving?

entries.summary: Closing the custom art style builder with unsaved changes now asks: Save, Don't save, or Keep editing.
entries.detail: Open a saved style, change an answer or a description (or click Rewrite), then close with the x: it asks. Keep editing leaves everything as it was on screen; Don't save closes and reopening shows the style as last saved; Save saves and closes. Open a style and close it without changing anything: it closes without asking. Generate a preview, then close: it does not ask (previews save themselves).

entries.summary: In the custom art style builder, click a reference image to see it larger. Replace sits beside Remove under each one.
entries.detail: Open the style builder. Click an empty reference box: the file picker opens. Click a box with a picture: it opens large, like pictures elsewhere; close it and nothing else has changed. Click Replace under a picture: the file picker opens and the new picture takes that box. Drag a picture onto a full box and onto an empty one: both take it. Open a saved style and check the same on its saved pictures.

entries.summary: The help assistant now knows the new custom art style builder: the 18 questions, Faithful, Bolder and Softer, the three preview scenes, the winner, and Convert to questions.
entries.detail: Ask the help assistant: How do I make a custom art style? What do Faithful, Bolder and Softer mean? My custom style does not look like my samples. How much does a custom style cost? Can a custom style make comic pages with several panels? (It should say not yet.) What happens to a style I made before?

entries.summary: Reference images in the custom art style builder show whole, fitted inside their boxes instead of cropped.
entries.detail: Open the style builder and add a tall and a wide reference image: each shows in full, scaled to fit, with the four boxes the same size as before.

entries.summary: The Outdoors style preview shows travellers on foot instead of wagons, which often came out with horses facing the wrong way.
entries.detail: Generate an Outdoors preview: three people walking a winding road through a wide valley toward a walled town on a far hill, under an evening sky. No wagons or horses.

entries.summary: Narrative styles other than Already Written write the Opening as they did before 3.1.65, so it no longer repeats itself.
entries.detail: Regenerate a prose narrative in a session that has a title picture (for example Epic Saga): the Opening should be one passage again, not a second paragraph restating the first. Already Written is unchanged: every sentence of the author's story still appears, the first ones in the Opening.

entries.summary: Style previews draw their people in the style's own way again: no more weathered, realistic faces in an anime style.
entries.detail: Generate a Close up in an anime style: one man in his thirties, no hood, dark hair showing, a dramatic startled expression, drawn with the style's own faces and eyes. The Group's four people should look like the style too. Faithful, Bolder and Softer should still show much the same people.

entries.summary: The custom art style answers are now a plain list: one line per question, hover to read the whole answer, Edit to change it.
entries.detail: Open a custom style with answers. Eighteen lines in two columns (one on a phone), in question order, no boxes and no groups. A long answer ends in an ellipsis; hovering shows it all. Edit opens a box on that line only; Done closes it and the line shows the new answer. Rewrite descriptions uses the edited answers.

entries.summary: The custom art style builder is easier to read: the answers are grouped summaries you click to edit, the three descriptions are Faithful, Bolder and Softer, and every wait shows a progress bar.
entries.detail: Open a custom style. The answers show as five groups (Drawing, Colour & light, Scene, Characters & energy, Anything else); click one to edit, Done to fold it. Labels are readable on white. The descriptions are labelled Faithful, Bolder and Softer and should look clearly different in strength. Generate a Close up: one person, closer in, in a square slot; Outdoors and Group in wide slots with no grey bars. The first Close up of Faithful, Bolder and Softer should show much the same man; Generate again draws a new one. Analyze, Rewrite, Convert and each picture show the red progress bar with a line of text.

entries.summary: Custom Art Styles have a new, bigger builder: 18 questions about how your style is drawn, three descriptions to compare, and preview pictures on three scenes for each.
entries.detail: Open Custom Art Styles. New style: add 2 to 4 reference images and Analyze (1 token). The 18 answers appear, then three descriptions, each with Close up, Outdoors and Group preview slots; Generate one picture at a time (1 token each, with the spinner). Use this one makes a description the winner: the other two grey out and freeze with their pictures, and Make this the winner swaps. Edit any answer and press Rewrite descriptions (free): if there is a winner it asks first. An older style opens with its paragraph and a Convert to questions button (free); nothing changes in your stories until you pick a winner. Close and reopen: everything is still there.

entries.summary: Behind the scenes: Analyze now answers 18 questions about how your samples are drawn and writes three descriptions from them. The screen to use them comes next.
entries.detail: On the current Custom Art Style screen: Analyze a style. The description that appears is the first of three now written from the 18 answers; it should name the background, where the detail goes, the finish, faces and figures and the energy, and state outright what the style does not have (no outlines, no glows). Existing styles and every book draw exactly as before. Preview still draws the old knight scene on this screen; the three new scenes arrive with the new screen.

entries.summary: Story text written beside a session's title picture now ends up in the Opening instead of being lost.
entries.detail: Already Written: generate a session that has a title picture. Every sentence of the story must appear, in order, with the first ones in the Opening (bots: rerun the 18-sentence Alpha to Romeo test). Any other style: regenerate a session that has a title picture. The Opening should set up the situation and lead into the story without describing the title picture, and nothing should be missing between the Opening and the first picture after it. Books are untouched until their narrative is generated again.

entries.summary: The Narrative button no longer names a narrator for Already Written.
entries.detail: On a version set to In first person with a narrator, switch the narrative style to Already Written. The Narrative button on the Storyboard, Review and Story tabs should read Narrative: Already Written, with no narrator. Switch back to another style: the narrator shows again.

entries.summary: The help assistant is now told exactly what the Redeem page offers your account for a gift, instead of working it out.
entries.detail: Ask: Why can't I take my gift as tokens? Erin (pass + live Gold): both choices; a pass pauses Gold, tokens leave it alone. Tamika (pass, Gold cancelling): both choices; the pass is added after hers. A real Free Trial: the pass only, no tokens. A Platinum subscriber: tokens only. Also check it no longer calls a pass holder a Platinum subscriber, and does not say a billing subscription restarts by itself.

entries.summary: The help assistant answers gift questions from your actual account, instead of assuming you are on the Free Trial or have a Platinum subscription.
entries.detail: Ask exactly: Why can't I take my gift as tokens? On an account that is Platinum through a pass (with or without a Silver/Gold subscription) it should say you can: the Redeem page offers Take tokens instead next to the pass. On a real Free Trial account it should say tokens cannot be added on the trial. On a Platinum subscriber it should say the gift is offered as tokens only. It must never call a pass holder a Platinum subscriber or say a paying account is on the Free Trial.

entries.summary: Gift payments in Stripe now show the Purchase ID, what was bought, who it is for, and the last 4 characters of the gift code.
entries.detail: Buy a gift, then find the payment in the Stripe dashboard. Its description should read like: Campaignia gift GIFT-18 · 3 months of Platinum · for Erin Bot · code ending AS6A, and its metadata should include purchase_id and code_last4. The last 4 must match the end of the code in the gift email. Resend a gift from the dashboard Gifts tab: the Stripe description should change to the new code's last 4. The full code never appears in Stripe.

entries.summary: The help assistant now knows whether your Platinum comes from a subscription or a pass, so it no longer tells a pass holder that a gift can only be taken as tokens.
entries.detail: Signed in on an account that is Platinum through a pass (no Platinum subscription), ask: Why can I not take my gift as a pass? or Can I take my gift as Platinum months? It should say you get both choices and the months are added after your pass. On a Platinum subscriber it should still say tokens only. Also ask: Am I on a subscription or a pass? and When does my pass end?

entries.summary: A gift whose payment is disputed or refunded is now cancelled even when Stripe reports it within seconds of the purchase.
entries.detail: Buy a gift with the dispute test card 4000 0000 0000 0259 and do not redeem it. Within a minute or two its code must say This gift has been cancelled. Before this, a dispute that arrived before the purchase had been recorded was missed and the code kept working (found by the bots on GIFT-12). Also check: a disputed gift sends no gift email if the dispute came first.

entries.summary: Every disputed payment, on any purchase, now emails support and the alert address with the amount, the reason, the evidence deadline and a link to it in Stripe.
entries.detail: Alerts are switched off on staging (ALERTS_ENABLED), so there a dispute writes a log line starting [alert suppressed: ALERTS_ENABLED!=true] Payment disputed instead. On production it emails both addresses. A disputed gift is named in the same email, with whether it was cancelled or already redeemed.

entries.summary: The help assistant now knows about gift certificates: giving one, redeeming one, and what a gifted pass does with each plan.
entries.detail: Ask the help assistant: how do I give Campaignia as a gift; do gifts expire; I am on Gold, will a gifted pass cancel my subscription; why can I not take my gift as tokens on the trial; my gift code is not recognised.

entries.summary: Internal: a code comment about gifted passes now says Silver and Gold subscriptions are paused.
entries.detail: Comment only, in services/gifts.js. Nothing anyone sees changes and there is nothing to test beyond the site still running.

entries.summary: On the Free Trial, the Redeem page no longer offers to take a pass gift as tokens, since the trial cannot hold them.
entries.detail: Redeem a pass gift on a Free Trial account: only the Redeem button shows, with its Platinum date and token total; there is no Take tokens instead button and no note under it. A Copper, Silver or Gold account still sees both choices. A token-pack gift on the trial still shows its button switched off with the reason.

entries.summary: The Redeem page's note under the two choices is shorter and no longer reads oddly for someone already on Platinum.
entries.detail: Redeem a pass gift as a Copper or Free Trial account: the note under the buttons reads only Choose one; it cannot be changed afterwards. Silver, Gold and Platinum subscribers keep their own notes, unchanged.

entries.summary: Each choice on the Redeem page now says what you would have after it.
entries.detail: Redeem a pass gift signed in. The Redeem button's small print reads Platinum until <date> and your new token total; for a Silver or Gold subscriber it adds, then Gold again (or Silver). Take tokens instead reads Bringing you to <total> tokens. A Platinum subscriber sees only the tokens choice. On the Free Trial the tokens choice is switched off and says tokens cannot be added during the Free Trial; a token-pack gift is switched off the same way. The date comes from the same code that sets it when you click, so it should match the result exactly. The account box now reads Currently, your account.

entries.summary: Redeeming a gift now shows your current plan and token balance, with end dates, before you choose how to take it.
entries.detail: Redeem page, signed in, after Check code: a Your account box between the gift and the buttons. Copper reads Copper; a subscription reads e.g. Gold subscription, renews <date> (or ends, or paused until); a pass adds Platinum Pass until <date>; the Free Trial reads Free Trial, ends <date> (N days left). The token count matches the app header. After redeeming, the box moves under the result as Your account now and shows the new pass date or balance. Signed out, no box.

entries.summary: After buying a gift, a Back to Campaignia link sits right beside Want to send another?
entries.detail: Buy a gift and return from Stripe: the line under the title reads Want to send another? followed by Back to Campaignia. It goes to the same place as the link at the bottom: the app when signed in, otherwise the landing page you came from.

entries.summary: Back to Campaignia on the Gift and Redeem pages takes you back where you were, and their field labels are easier to read.
entries.detail: Signed in, it opens the app. Signed out, it goes back to the page you came from: the storyteller page or the game page. That still works after a Stripe checkout or a sign-in. Opened from an email link, it goes to the home page. The name, email, message and gift code labels are also brighter on the dark background.

entries.summary: Saying thanks or perfect to the help assistant no longer shows Could not answer that right now.
entries.detail: With the end-of-help email switched on, the assistant sometimes answered a thank-you with only its hidden end marker, which left an empty reply and showed an error with your word put back in the box. It now says a short goodbye instead, and the end-of-help email is sent as intended (it was being skipped in exactly these cases). The assistant is also told to always write a closing line before the marker. Separately, when the email service refused a help transcript email, nothing said so and the page was told it had gone; a refusal is now logged with the reason and the address it was meant for.

entries.summary: The word counts and the help lines under the story and instructions boxes on the Story tab are readable now.
entries.detail: The word counts were dark brown on near-black and could not be seen; the help lines and the saves-automatically note were dim. All of them are lighter and a touch larger, each with a contrast of at least 4.5 to 1. The amber colour for a story past the Already Written limit is unchanged.

entries.summary: The Narrative and Art style buttons are on the Story tab too, beside Generate Story, so a style can be chosen before the first generation. Already Written now recommends a length and asks before generating a story longer than that.
entries.detail: On the Story tab the two buttons sit beside Generate Story, as on Review and Storyboard. With Already Written chosen, the word count under the story box adds: Already Written: up to 3,000 a session, and turns amber past it. Past it, Generate Story and Generate Narrative ask first (Continue anyway or Go back); nothing is refused and nothing is charged until you continue. The number is a dashboard setting: Dashboard > Settings > Generation charging > Already Written, recommended words per session (default 3,000, about a chapter). The Already Written card names the number. On a phone the two style buttons share Generate Story's row, showing just the style names (the full label is the tooltip). Also: the Import from file button is shorter, so the story box and the instructions box now start at the same height.

entries.summary: Both landing pages now say Campaignia can do it all, or you can: We do it all, Illustrate it yourself, Write it yourself.
entries.detail: A new band right after the features strip on the game page (Play it your way) and the storyteller page (Tell it your way), three across on a desktop and stacked on a phone, ending with: Artist, writer, or neither, we've got you covered. Each page has its own slant: an artist at the table and a DM's campaign journal on one; family photos, a child's drawings and an already-written story on the other. One new FAQ on each page, full width at the end. Write it yourself is the Already Written narrative style (3.1.49).

entries.summary: A new narrative style, Already Written: your own finished story, kept word for word and split around the pictures. Campaignia writes nothing new.
entries.detail: Put a finished story in the Story / Session Transcript box, choose Narrative style > Already Written (last in the list, every plan), then Generate Story and Generate Narrative. Every narrative panel holds your own sentences, in order, each used once; cuts fall between sentences. A panel can be empty where two pictures come one after the other in the text. Narrative length and In first person are greyed out for this style and come back as they were on any other. It costs the usual Generate Narrative tokens. Also fixed: in the tall-picture layouts, a narrative panel that is empty no longer prints the picture's internal description in its place (that note is only used now when the book has no narrative at all).

entries.summary: On a phone the gift notice no longer adds a strip under the header: a small gift icon sits on the corner of the account button, and the account menu's first line says Someone gave you a gift.
entries.detail: Ian: it must not take up any more vertical space. On a phone (640px and narrower) the header has no room for the badge, so the gift is an icon pinned to the corner of the account button (tap it to redeem) and the top line of the account menu. The header is the same height and width as for an account with no gift. On a wider screen nothing changed: SOMEONE GAVE YOU A GIFT in the header, now also on the top line of the account menu.

entries.summary: Gifts: the buyer's receipt carries the gift code, the buyer is emailed when the gift is redeemed, and the person it was sent to sees a Someone gave you a gift badge at the top of Campaignia until they redeem it.
entries.detail: Gifts must be switched on. Buy a gift (Stripe test card) for an address that has a Campaignia account: the receipt now shows the code, even for a gift dated in the future, and that same code is the one in the gift email on the day. The buyer's copy of the code says they will hear when it is redeemed. Sign in as the recipient once the gift's day has come: the header shows SOMEONE GAVE YOU A GIFT (GIFT on a phone); click it, redeem, and the badge is gone. The badge only counts the email address the account confirmed at sign-up, never one typed into the profile later. When the recipient redeems, the buyer gets an email saying so (not for free gifts, and not when the buyer redeems it). New email previews: Gift - buyer told it was redeemed.

entries.summary: Gift certificates, part two: anyone can buy a Platinum Pass or a token pack as a gift from a Give Campaignia page, with a button below the tiers on both landing pages.
entries.detail: Gifts must be switched on (Dashboard > Gifts) or none of this shows. Test with a Stripe test card: open /gift signed out, pick a pass, fill in a recipient you can read, pay. You should get a receipt (no code on it), the recipient gets the gift email, and you get a copy of the code. Try a delivery date (paid now, sent at 9am Eastern that day). Try a 4th purchase from the same email within 24 hours (refused). On the Gifts tab a paid gift shows its price and Void & refund (refunds in Stripe and kills the code; refused once redeemed). Walking away from checkout marks the gift Checkout abandoned once Stripe expires the session. For refunds made in the Stripe dashboard to void a gift, the webhook endpoint must have charge.refunded and charge.dispute.created switched on. Also fixed: the pass panel on My Account no longer tells subscribers their subscription keeps billing.

entries.summary: Buying a Platinum Pass no longer ends a Silver or Gold subscription: Platinum starts at once and the subscription is paused until the pass ends, then restarts by itself.
entries.detail: Test in Stripe test mode. Gold subscriber buys a pass: the dialog says Gold will be paused (Buy the pass / Not yet). After paying: Platinum now, My Account shows Billing paused until the pass end date, the Stripe subscription shows payment collection paused until that date (invoices voided), no Gold charge meanwhile, and the receipt says Gold paused until DATE. Buy a second pass while paused: the pause moves to the new end date. Platinum subscriber buys a pass: a confirmation that the subscription stops renewing (as before). A gifted pass redeemed by a Gold subscriber offers Platinum now (Gold paused) or the tokens. If Stripe refuses a pause, the pass is still granted and Ian gets an email.

entries.summary: Redeeming a gift on an account with a different email from the one it was sent to now shows a warning, but still lets you redeem.
entries.detail: Send a free gift to one address, then open its Redeem link signed in as a different account: an amber note names the address it was sent to (masked, e.g. a***@example.com) and the account you are signed in as. Redeem still works. Signed in with the matching address (any capitals), no note. Signed out, nothing is shown.

entries.summary: A gifted pass now fits the subscription it lands on: Platinum subscribers take the tokens, Silver and Gold subscribers get Platinum starting today with their subscription untouched, and a gift never ends a subscription.
entries.detail: Test on staging with three accounts. Platinum subscriber: the Redeem page offers only Take tokens (the pass is refused even if forced). Gold subscriber: Platinum now for the pass's months plus its tokens, or the tokens; choosing Platinum makes them Platinum today, the Gold subscription is unchanged and keeps billing, and they return to Gold when the pass ends. No subscription, or one already set to cancel: the pass as before (it starts after any paid-up period). Pausing the subscription during a pass comes in 3.1.45.

entries.summary: Gift certificates, part one: a Gifts tab on the dashboard with an on/off switch, free gifts sent by email (now or on a date), and a Redeem page where a gifted pass can be kept or taken as tokens.
entries.detail: Gifts are OFF until switched on in Dashboard > Gifts, separately on each server. To test: switch on, send yourself a free 3-month pass, open the email's Redeem link, sign in and redeem; the pass and 200 tokens land on your account. Send another pass and choose Take tokens instead (list price divided by the Pass to tokens rate, 20 cents to start, e.g. 395 for the 3-month pass). Try the link again (already redeemed), a token pack on a Free Trial account (refused, gift kept), Resend (old code stops working), Void, and a dated gift (sent at 9am Eastern that day). Buying gifts comes in part two.

entries.summary: The help assistant's answers show bold and italics properly instead of stray asterisks.
The story box's placeholder and the line under it no longer assume a transcript.
entries.detail: It now invites a transcript, a written story, notes or an outline, and says your story and notes save automatically.

entries.summary: Making a version the Canonical now warns at the top of the window when any of its sessions are Draft.
entries.detail: Members only see sessions set to Ready. The warning names every Draft session, and says so plainly when the whole version is Draft.

entries.summary: Members who can't publish are no longer offered All publishing options on a session's Preview, and an invitation with no character no longer says Playing as null.
The session arrows' tooltips name the previous and next session.
entries.detail: They read .title, which sessions don't have; they use the name, or the date when there is none.

entries.summary: Messages about the story box no longer assume a transcript.
entries.detail: An empty or very short Story / Session Transcript box, the saved message and the Generate Story progress line now talk about your story: a transcript, a written story, notes or an outline all work.

entries.summary: The help assistant now explains what the Canonical is, what order sessions come in, and where the Outline warnings appear.
entries.detail: Also: an empty transcript box now says 'Please paste a transcript first.'

entries.summary: On the session page, two sessions on the same date now show the one made last first.
entries.detail: The session page reads newest first and Publish and the book read oldest first; same-date sessions now follow each page's direction, and the session arrows follow the cards.

entries.summary: Open on a Publish session card now opens the version you were looking at.
entries.detail: It used to open your pinned version. It now opens that version's copy of the session, or the Canonical where the version never made the session its own, as the card says.

entries.summary: Two sessions on the same date now appear in the order they were made, in the list, on Publish and in the book.
Delete This Session From This Version is no longer offered on the Canonical; the promote window no longer promises Story Instructions carry to new sessions.
entries.detail: Story Instructions belong to each session. The 3.1.35 entry and the Brain were corrected.

entries.summary: In first person now wins over Story Instructions that ask for the third person, and says so.
entries.detail: When In first person is ticked, the story is told as 'I' even if the Story Instructions ask for third person; the rest of the instructions are still followed. The Narrative style window warns when your instructions mention point of view.

entries.summary: A session's Preview now explains when Outline bullet points are still in it.
entries.detail: The same warning as Prep & Preview: in the book the bullets run together as one paragraph, so replace them with your own words before you Optimize.

entries.summary: Small fixes: the Opening badge on Review, long version names in the picker, and clearer messages.
entries.detail: The Opening badge on the Review tab no longer spills into the title. Long version names wrap in the version picker instead of being cut short. The missing-transcript message no longer says your transcript is gone. The reference-picture message says 'they' for more than one character, and the Story Instructions hint says notes save when you click away.

entries.summary: Promote to Canonical no longer freezes other versions with copies of the old pages.
entries.detail: Ian: take out the freezing. Other versions follow the new Canonical on sessions they never branched. The promoted version still gets every session. The 3.1.35 entry was reworded.

entries.summary: Story Masters can make one of their own versions the Canonical, and carry on in its style.
entries.detail: Open the version, click the ... menu and choose Make This Version the Canonical. Members read it from now on and new sessions start in its art style and narrative style. Sessions it never had are copied in from the old Canonical as they are. Other versions show the new Canonical on any session they haven't made their own. The old Canonical is kept under a new name, or deleted after a second confirmation. Published stories and orders are not affected.

entries.summary: The summary carried into the next session now comes from the same version's previous session.
entries.detail: inheritedSummary took the caller's first fork by id, which with several versions could hand one version another's memory, and after a promote would have picked the old Canonical.

entries.summary: Both version pickers are now drawn by Campaignia, with a pin on every row; the separate star is gone.
entries.detail: The native select stays hidden as the source of truth, so switching, the in-flight locks and the change handlers are unchanged. The 3.1.33 entry was reworded from star to pin.

entries.summary: Pin a version to make it your default: it's the one that opens whenever you come to the campaign.
entries.detail: Open the version picker on the session page or the Publish page and click the pin at the end of a version's row; click it again to unpin. One per person per campaign. On a session your pinned version never branched, you see the canonical there, just as the book does. Pinning changes no book and nothing anyone else sees.

entries.summary: In first person: 'Nobody in particular (just I)' is now a choice on every narrative style.
entries.detail: The Narrator list always offers Nobody in particular: the story is told as 'I' with no character named as the narrator, and nobody is featured in the pictures. If you tick In first person and close the window without choosing, that is what is saved. Choose a character instead to have them named in the pictures and appear in more of them.
