entries.summary: Prep & Preview warns when a book still holds Outline bullet points.
entries.detail: If any session in the book still has narrative written as Outline / I'll write it bullets, Prep & Preview names those sessions and explains that bullets print as one run-together paragraph, so they can be replaced before you Optimize.

entries.summary: First person: the style button names the narrator; Calm & Literal can choose nobody; the Opening panel gets its art brief.
entries.detail: The Narrative button reads e.g. 'Epic Saga · Narrator: Beth'. On Calm & Literal the Narrator list offers 'Nobody in particular (just I)' so the saved choice is visible and changeable there. With In first person ticked, the window cannot be closed until a narrator is chosen (or the box is unticked). After Generate Story the saved panels are reloaded, so the Opening picture panel appears straight away and, on a Self Illustrated version, shows its art brief. The art brief's heading now sits below the hover buttons.

entries.summary: Testers and admins see the version stamp at the foot of the profile menu on a phone.
entries.detail: The header stamp stays hidden on phones for space; the same text now appears at the bottom of the profile menu there, so a finding from a phone can name its version.

entries.summary: I'll illustrate it myself: a switch in the Art style window for books where you supply every picture.
entries.detail: Art style window, new I'll illustrate it myself switch (per version, every plan). Campaignia then draws no pictures for that version and spends no image tokens; each empty picture panel shows an art brief (what to draw, the panel's shape, who is in it with their descriptions, the look to aim for) with Upload your own on it. Pictures already on panels stay. The book is labelled Self Illustrated.

entries.summary: Every picture you upload onto a panel is now labelled Self Illustrated.
entries.detail: On the panel, in the Archive and in the Library, whether or not the rest of the book was drawn by Campaignia. Pictures uploaded earlier are labelled too. The Library's art style filter has a Self Illustrated option. Revert on an uploaded picture puts back the earlier picture's own label.

entries.summary: Custom Art Style Builder: the note about mixed results moved onto an i beside Reference images.
entries.detail: The paragraph under the reference image slots (the AI reads the rendering style across your samples; image models have their own tendencies, so results can be mixed) is now on a circled i next to the Reference images label: hover on a desktop, tap on a phone. Same text.

entries.summary: Narrative style window: In first person sits beside Narrative length, the explanations moved onto an i icon, and the whole window scrolls.
entries.detail: The In first person switch and Narrator list share one row with the Low/Med/High length control (they stack on a narrow phone), without the surrounding box. The descriptions under In first person and Narrative length moved onto a circled i beside each (hover on a desktop, tap on a phone). The whole Narrative style window now scrolls as one, controls included, instead of only the cards scrolling under fixed controls; the art and layout pickers are unchanged. The note under it keeps only: the narrative is told as the narrator, as 'I', and the narrator appears in more pictures.

entries.summary: Tell a story in the first person: pick a narrator at the top of the Narrative style window.
entries.detail: Narrative style window, new In first person switch with a Narrator list (any character, Supporting Characters / NPCs included). The narrative is told as that character, as 'I', and they appear in more pictures than the other characters. It works with every narrative style and outranks the Story Instructions. Calm & Literal is always first person; Adventurer's Journal turns it on when chosen and can be switched off. A narrator is required while it is on. It belongs to the version and carries into its next sessions. Takes effect at the next Generate Story and Generate Narrative. Every plan.

entries.summary: New narrative style, Outline / I'll write it: bullet points you write your own story over.
entries.detail: Each narrative panel gets bullet points instead of prose: what happens, who is there, the key moment and a line of dialogue worth keeping. Low, Med and High set how many bullets. Pictures are drawn as usual. Every plan. Bullets left in a printed book print as one paragraph, so replace them before ordering.

entries.summary: On a phone, the tester badge shortens to 'Platinum · Test' so the page no longer scrolls sideways.
entries.detail: Tester accounts, phone width (under about 600px): the header badge reads e.g. 'Platinum · Test' instead of 'Platinum, Test Account (Not Billed)', the page fits the screen and the profile menu is reachable. Desktop unchanged; the tooltip and the click to testing controls are unchanged.

entries.summary: New example sentences for the Lorekeeper / Historian and Adventurer's Journal narrative styles, in the style picker and in what the AI is shown.
entries.detail: Narrative style picker: Lorekeeper / Historian now reads 'Of the Siege of Hollowmere...' and Adventurer's Journal 'Day six. My boots have given up...'. The same sentences are the model examples the AI imitates, so stories in those two voices lose the old joke tone. Generate Narrative in each voice to compare.

entries.summary: The help assistant now knows about uploading your own panel pictures, the cover and asset framing, iPhone photos, and importing characters from another campaign.
entries.detail: Help, ask: how do I use my own art on a panel; can I choose which part goes on the cover; can I make an asset from part of an archived picture; can I bring a character from another campaign; why was my upload cropped. Each should get the steps and rules as shipped in 3.1.14 to 3.1.23.

entries.summary: Import a character from another campaign you belong to, choosing any look they have had there.
entries.detail: Characters page, the new Import from another campaign tile (Story Master): choose one of your other campaigns (ones you run or belong to), then a character, then a picture. The pictures are the character's original card, then every look from each version of that campaign you can see, oldest first; groups load as you scroll. Import copies the character into this campaign with that look: its own copy of every picture, so changing either campaign never affects the other. Who plays the character does not carry over, and it counts toward this campaign's character limit. If the name is already used here, a number is added.

entries.summary: Generate Story now tells you which characters have no reference picture yet, so they can be built before the story is drawn.
entries.detail: Story tab, Generate Story, in a campaign whose characters include one with no reference picture: a message names them and explains that the reference is what keeps a character looking the same. Build References goes to the Characters page (Story Master, or the character's owner); Generate Now carries on. It asks every time while any are missing. A campaign with no characters at all still gets the original question once.

entries.summary: Support access shows the last five customer emails you viewed as; one click puts one back in the box.
entries.detail: Admin, Support access: under the email box, Recent: lists up to five different customer emails from the support log, newest first. Clicking one fills the email box (it does not start the session). Nothing new is stored; it reads the same log as Recent support sessions.

entries.summary: Guided tours no longer start by themselves while an admin is viewing as a customer.
entries.detail: Admin, Support access: start a session as a customer whose tours have not been seen and move around the app: no tour pops up. The customer's own tour history is not changed (a tour opened by hand is not recorded as seen). End the session and tours behave as before for your own account.

entries.summary: Browsers no longer fill your email into filter and search boxes; autofill is kept only for My Account and the shipping address.
entries.detail: On a phone, the Archive's Moment Name filter could arrive filled with your email address and show nothing until cleared. My Account's profile and password now sit in their own forms, every other text box is marked not to autofill, and the filter boxes ignore text nobody typed. The shipping address on the Order tab still offers your saved address. Also: framing a cover on a phone now fits the picture to the screen and keeps the buttons in view.

entries.summary: The cover framing window now fits on the screen: no scroll bar, and the buttons are always visible.
entries.detail: Publish, Cover or Back Cover, choose a picture that opens the frame: the picture is sized to the window so the frame, the size line or warning, and Back to the Archive / Use this framing all show without scrolling. Try it with a small picture (two-line warning) and on a short window.

entries.summary: Choosing a front or back cover picture from the Archive now lets you frame exactly which part of the picture goes on the cover.
entries.detail: Publish, Cover or Back Cover, choose a picture: unless it is already the cover's shape, it opens with a cover-shaped frame, placed where the cover would have cut it before. Drag the frame to move it, drag a corner to zoom in, then Use this framing. A frame under 750 pixels tall shows the orange small-picture warning (you can still use it). Pictures that are already cover-shaped, and picking the current cover to remove it, work exactly as before. The title-page picture is unchanged.

entries.summary: Copy to Assets from the Archive now lets you frame just the part of the picture you want as the asset.
entries.detail: Archive, Copy to Assets: the picture appears with a frame round the whole of it. Drag a corner to change the frame's size and shape freely, drag the frame to move it; only the framed part becomes the asset (the archived picture is not changed). Leave the frame round the whole picture to copy it as before. The upload-your-own crop on a panel now uses the same frame and should behave exactly as in 3.1.16.

entries.summary: When you upload your own picture onto a panel, the crop frame now has corner handles: zoom in on just the part you want and move it anywhere.
entries.detail: Replace on a panel, Upload your own: after choosing a picture, drag the frame to move it in any direction and drag a corner to make it smaller or larger (the shape stays the same, the opposite corner stays put). The size line and warning update as you drag; the small-picture warning is now the orange warning box used elsewhere. Use this image stores exactly the framed area. Try zooming in far on a large photo (warning appears), then back out (it goes away). Picking another shape starts again from the largest frame.

entries.summary: Put your own picture on a storyboard panel: Replace now has an Upload your own tab. Campaignia fits it to the panel shape it suits best, and you can slide the crop.
entries.detail: Storyboard, any panel's Replace pill: two tabs, From Archive (as before) and Upload your own. The upload tab shows the seven panel shapes, a drop zone with the usual rights line, and after a file is chosen a crop preview in the shape the picture fits best (click another shape to change it; drag the frame to choose what is kept). A picture under 1024 pixels on its long side once cropped shows a warning and can still be used. Use this image: the panel takes the new shape, the picture is stored at that exact ratio (up to 2048 px), the panel is LOCKED (Generate Images skips it; unlock to retouch), and the previous picture is in Revert -- unlock, Revert, and the old picture AND its old shape come back. JPG, PNG, WebP and HEIC, up to 20 MB, any tier, no tokens. Replacing from the Archive now also remembers the shape for Revert. Other pickers (characters, assets, cover, Title Builder) show no upload tab.

entries.summary: iPhone photos (HEIC) can now be uploaded for characters and assets; Campaignia converts them to JPG for you.
entries.detail: Upload a .heic from an iPhone as a character portrait (any of the four slots), as an asset picture, and in the bulk asset import. In Chrome or Edge the preview should appear after a moment (it is converted on the server first; Chrome cannot show HEIC itself), and the saved image is a JPG. Railway log: one [heic] converted line per file. A file named .heic that is not really one is refused with a clear message. NEW DEPENDENCY heic-convert (WebAssembly, no native build): if the staging deploy fails to build, that is the cause, and the previous version keeps running.

entries.summary: Click an asset pill on the Review or Storyboard tab to see that asset's picture without leaving the page.
entries.detail: Review tab and the Storyboard panel options: clicking an asset pill opens its picture full size in the lightbox, captioned with its name and category (Escape or a click outside closes it). Clicking the x on the pill still only removes it from the panel and does not open the picture. A pill whose asset has no picture yet says so; an automatically matched pill without an id is found by name.

entries.summary: You can edit the description of each suggested asset before choosing Yes or No.
entries.detail: Each suggestion in the modal now has an editable description. Yes draws the asset from the edited text (check the new asset's description in the Asset Library); No, or unticking, puts the edited text into those panels' image prompts (the RECURRING ELEMENTS line in the Generate Images debug log). A blank box keeps the original. Members who cannot create assets can still edit, and OK saves their edits for their own version's panels. The boxes lock once Yes is clicked.

entries.summary: Suggested assets now describe how things look rather than what they do, and things you mention in your Story Instructions count when they are ranked.
entries.detail: Three follow-ups from Ian's mirror test. (1) Descriptions: Generate Story is told to describe appearance at rest only -- no powers, uses, glowing or activated states -- so an asset picture does not bake one scene's effect into every panel. Check a magic item's suggested description reads as a plain object. (2) Ranking counts mentions in the Story Instructions as well as the transcript; the 2-panel rule is unchanged. (3) Diagnostics: every Generate Story writes one [asset-suggest] line to the Railway log listing each candidate the model offered, whether it was kept, and why not (already an asset or character, matched only N panels, past the top 8, and so on), with panel numbers and mention counts. With debug mode on, the same list is in the Debug panel under Generate Story.

entries.summary: While Campaignia draws your suggested assets, each one shows a spinner that turns into its picture, with a progress bar for the set.
entries.detail: Ian, testing 3.1.9: the modal gave no sign it was working. Generate Story on a session with suggestions, tick two or more, click Yes: every ticked row shows the same gold spinner the panels use, each turns into its thumbnail as it lands, and the gold bar above the message fills as they finish. Unticked rows dim and the checkboxes lock. A suggestion that failed to start says so on its row.

entries.summary: After Generate Story, Campaignia suggests the people, places and things that appear in more than one panel, and can create them as assets for you so they look the same every time.
entries.detail: Run Generate Story on a session where something recurs (a named place, a supporting character, an item) in two or more panels. On landing on Review a modal lists up to 8, ranked by how often the transcript mentions them, each with a checkbox, its category, its panel count and a description. The token total updates as you untick; it refuses up front if the total is more than your balance or more than the tier's asset room. Yes creates the ticked ones (1 token each on success) and waits for the pictures; they then show as asset pills on the Review panels that name them. No, or unticking, keeps the description and adds it to those panels' image prompts (see the finalPrompt in the Generate Images debug log: RECURRING ELEMENTS). Things that look like main characters are listed as a Characters-tab suggestion only. Re-run Generate Story: already-made assets are not suggested again. As a member: without Allow Members to Add Assets you see the list and an OK only. Existing assets and Generate Story otherwise behave as before.

entries.summary: An open book on the Bookshelf now shows its subtitle, how many sessions it holds, its art and narrative styles, and its campaign's genres.
entries.detail: Ian: on the inside of a book opened from the Bookshelf, show the subtitle, how many sessions it is, the art and narrative style stored with that version, and the campaign's genres. A book saved from now on records these when you press Save to Bookshelf, so it keeps describing what it holds even if the version changes later. Books already on shelves are filled in once, from their version as it is now, the first time you open the Bookshelf. When a book's sessions use more than one style, all of them are listed. A Library book shows the genres and art styles its story was published with. TO TEST: open a book on the Bookshelf: the subtitle sits under the title in italics; the layout line ends with the number of sessions; Art, Narrative and Genre lines follow. A book whose sessions mix styles lists each style once. A Library book shows its Genre and Art lines. Save a new book and check the same lines appear.

entries.summary: Field labels on the Feedback and My Account pages are sharp again, and every page title now reads in gold on the darker background.
entries.detail: Ian: the Feedback page's labels (Type, Subject, Message) looked blurry. 3.1.6 gave every field label a dark edge so it would read over the background's candles, but on white cards that edge blurred dark lettering. The edge now applies to field labels only on the session page, where they sit straight on the background; everywhere else labels are as crisp as before. Titles, subtitles, dates and tab names keep their edge. Ian also spotted that the My Account heading had become almost invisible: some pages still drew their title in the old dark lettering, which the darker background swallowed. Every page title is now gold and the line under it cream. TO TEST: My Account and Feedback: the page title reads gold and the line under it cream; Feedback and My Account: the field labels are crisp. A session page: Story / Session Transcript still has its dark edge and reads clearly over the candles.

entries.summary: The background picture is darker on every page, and page titles, tabs and labels have a soft dark edge, so the gold lettering no longer disappears into the candlelight.
entries.detail: Ian: with the dark panels gone, the candle flames in the background picture were the same gold as the page's lettering, and words crossing them were lost. Ian chose 70% from previews at 30, 40, 50 and 70. The background is now 70% darker on every page, the same picture in the same place, and the words that sit straight on it (page titles and subtitles, dates, tab names and field labels) have a soft dark edge that keeps them readable even over a flame. Panels, cards, buttons and the book previews are unchanged. TO TEST: a session page, a campaign's Sessions page, My Campaigns, My Stuff, Publish and the Dashboard: the background is dim but still visible, and every title, tab name and label reads clearly, including where it crosses a candle.

entries.summary: The dark panel behind the Sessions, session, Characters, Publish, Asset Library and Dashboard pages is gone, so every page shows the same background.
entries.detail: Ian: remove the dark panel from the sessions page and the session page, and everywhere else it appears. Six pages drew a dark, blurred panel over the background picture: a campaign's Sessions page, a session's own page, Characters, Publish, the Asset Library and the Dashboard. That panel is now off on all of them, as it already is on My Campaigns and My Stuff, so the whole app sits on one background. The panels and cards inside those pages keep their own dark backgrounds. TO TEST: open each of those six pages and check the words directly on the background (page titles, subtitles, tab names, hints) are still easy to read; if any are not, the panel can be switched back or the background darkened for every page.

entries.summary: My Campaigns now sits on the same background as the rest of the app, without the dark panel behind the campaign books.
entries.detail: Ian: My Campaigns looked darker than My Stuff, as if a dark panel sat behind it. It did: the page drew its own copy of the background picture with a dark layer over it. That layer and the extra copy are gone, so My Campaigns shows the same background as every other page, and the line under the title is a little brighter with a shadow so it stays readable. TO TEST: My Campaigns: no dark box behind the books; the background matches My Stuff; the title, subtitle, book names and New campaign are all easy to read. If they are not, it can be switched back.

entries.summary: Admin: the number of Bookshelf books each tier keeps is now a field on the Dashboard's Tiers and Passes tab.
entries.detail: Ian: a field on each tier panel to control how many Bookshelf entries that tier gets, with the help Brain reading from it. Every tier panel on Dashboard, Tiers and Passes now has Bookshelf books (0 = no Bookshelf); it starts at today's numbers (Gold 10, Platinum 50, the others 0) and a change takes effect straight away, as the other tier fields do. Everything that named the plans and numbers now reads the setting: the Bookshelf tab's upgrade note, the message when a plan without a Bookshelf tries to save or add a Library book, and the help assistant, whose live tier numbers now include each tier's Bookshelf size and whose Brain no longer states fixed numbers. Books already on a shelf are never removed by lowering a number: over the limit, people can view, download, bring back and remove, but not add. TO TEST: Dashboard, Tiers and Passes: every tier panel shows Bookshelf books; Gold reads 10 and Platinum 50. Set Silver to 3 and save: a Silver account's Bookshelf tab shows 0 of 3 books and Save to Bookshelf works; the upgrade note on a Copper account now names Silver too; ask the help assistant how many books Silver can keep: 3. Put Silver back to 0.

entries.summary: The help assistant now knows about My Stuff, the Bookshelf and the new order cards, and sends people to the right place for their orders and published stories.
entries.detail: Ian: update the Brain for My Stuff, My Orders and the Bookshelf. The help assistant's knowledge now covers My Stuff and its three tabs: My Orders (the cover, details, Check with the printer, Reorder this book, and Delete on unpaid checkouts), the Bookshelf (Save to Bookshelf from Optimize, Gold 10 / Platinum 50, Library books that do not count, Bring back to Publish and when it cannot, what happens on a downgrade) and Published Stories. Everywhere it used to send people to My Stories on the Account page now points to My Stuff, Published Stories. New answers: how to keep a finished book without ordering or publishing it, where orders and published stories are, what to do when a paid order seems stuck, and why a book cannot be saved or brought back. TO TEST: ask the help assistant: where are my orders; how do I keep my book without ordering it; why can't I save to my Bookshelf; where do I change my published story to public. Each answer should name My Stuff and the right tab.

entries.summary: The ... menu button on each session book is now gold and easy to see.
entries.detail: Ian: the dots on the session tile's menu button could not be seen. The button shared the app's standard dark colour, which disappeared on the dark book cover. On the session books it is now gold with a gold edge, brightening when you point at it. TO TEST: a campaign's Sessions page: every book's ... button shows gold dots; it opens the menu and Delete session still asks first.

entries.summary: Session book pictures are back to their larger size, trimmed neatly at the gold border instead of shrunk to fit inside it.
entries.detail: Ian: keep the pictures blown up as they were, and just trim the sides so they do not go outside the gold lines. Each session's picture is its larger size again, centred in the upper part of the cover; its sides are now cut cleanly at the gold line, so nothing crosses it, and its top and bottom still fade into the cover. TO TEST: a campaign's Sessions page and Publish > Session: pictures as large as in 3.0.998; their left and right edges stop exactly at the gold line on every book; controls still work.

entries.summary: Session book pictures now stay inside the gold border instead of running over it.
entries.detail: Ian: keep the picture on a session book from bleeding over the gold trim line. Each session's picture now spans exactly the inside of the gold line, still centred in the upper part of the cover with its edges faded, and a tall picture stops short of the line at the top as well. TO TEST: a campaign's Sessions page and Publish > Session: no picture crosses the gold line on any side; pictures still centred and faded; controls still work.

entries.summary: Session books now match the campaign books more closely: the picture is larger and centred, the gold border runs all the way round, and New campaign has a binding too.
entries.detail: Ian, from the first look at the session books: the pictures sat at the top leaving a gap, and the gold line faded out along the bottom. Each session's picture is now a little larger, centred in the upper part of the cover, with its foot under the dark fade that carries the words. The gold line is drawn above everything, so it runs unbroken round all four sides. The New campaign blank book gains the same shaded binding as the others. TO TEST: a campaign's Sessions page and Publish > Session: pictures centred and filling more of the cover; the gold line unbroken along the bottom; controls still work. My Campaigns: the New campaign book has the binding down its left edge.

entries.summary: Session tiles are hardback books too, on a campaign's Sessions page and on the Session tab under Publish, to match the campaign books.
entries.detail: Ian: do the same for the session tiles as the campaign books. On a campaign's Sessions page and on the Session tab under Publish, each session is now a dark 8.5 x 11 cover with the binding shaded down the left and a thin gold line inside its edge; its picture sits at the top, faded into a soft wash of itself, and a dark fade at the foot carries the tile's words and controls: the name and date, Ready or Draft and the menu on the Sessions page; the version, panel count, Ready or Draft, Include in Print and Open on the Session tab. Nothing a tile does has changed. TO TEST: a campaign's Sessions page: every session is a book; clicking one opens it; the ... menu still opens and Delete session still asks; a session with no picture shows the plain cover. Publish, Session tab: every session is a book; Include in Print still ticks and saves; Open still opens the session; a drawn chapter title shows whole. Narrow the window and both reflow. The previous tiles come back by setting SESSION_CARDS_AS_BOOKS to false in app.js.

entries.summary: A long session description now shows as a short snippet on the session page, with the full text when you hover over it, the same as campaign descriptions.
entries.detail: Ian: some people paste whole books into a session's description, which pushed the rest of the session page down. The session page now shows the first part of a long description, cut at a word and ending in an ellipsis, and hovering over it shows all of it, exactly as the campaign description does on the Sessions page. Short descriptions are unchanged, and editing a session still opens the whole description. TO TEST: give a session a very long description: the session page shows about two lines ending in an ellipsis; hover to read all of it; click the edit pencil: the full text is in the box; save a short one: it shows in full with no hover text.

entries.summary: My Campaigns shows each campaign as a hardback book: its picture faded into a dark cover with a gold border, and the name and details along the bottom.
entries.detail: Ian: make the campaign cards look like hardback book covers, like the books facing out on the Bookshelf. Each campaign is now a dark cover in the proportions of our 8.5 x 11 books, shaded down the left edge like a binding, with a thin gold line inside its edge. The campaign's picture, whatever its shape, is faded into the cover, and a dark fade over its foot carries the campaign name, description, date and the Details button. A campaign with no picture shows the logo faded in. New campaign is a blank book with a dashed gold border. Clicking a book opens the campaign as before. TO TEST: My Campaigns: every campaign is a book; wide, square and tall pictures all sit inside the cover without hard edges; the text reads on the dark fade; Details still opens the campaign's details and does not open the campaign; New campaign still opens the form; narrow the window and the books reflow. The previous cards come back by setting CAMPAIGN_CARDS_AS_BOOKS to false in app.js.

entries.summary: My Published Stories goes dark to match My Orders: the tiles are dark panels with gold lettering, and the white card behind them is gone.
entries.detail: Ian: reverse the colours on the Published Stories tab the way My Orders was done, keeping the tiles' size and look. The white card behind the tiles is gone, as on the Bookshelf tab; the heading and its description sit on a dark strip in gold and cream; each tile is a dark panel with a gold edge, and its title, date, blurb and buttons keep their light colours, which now read clearly. Nothing about what the tiles do has changed. TO TEST: My Stuff, Published Stories: no white card; the heading reads gold on dark; every tile is dark with a gold edge, the cover on top as before; Edit, Make link only / Make public, Copy link and Remove from Library all still work; with no stories, the empty line reads on a dark strip.

entries.summary: My Stuff's Back button goes to My Campaigns whenever it cannot tell where you came from.
entries.detail: Ian: if Back on My Stuff does not know exactly where you were, go to My Campaigns. Back still returns to the page you opened My Stuff from when it knows it (a campaign's Sessions, Characters, the book, My Campaigns, My Account). When it does not, or you came from a campaign page but no campaign is open any more, it now goes to My Campaigns instead of trying to show a campaign's Sessions. It also no longer borrows a return point left behind by an earlier Asset Library or Archives visit. TO TEST: open My Stuff from My Campaigns, from inside a campaign, and from My Account: Back returns to each. Reload the page and open My Stuff straight away: Back goes to My Campaigns.

entries.summary: The Bookshelf loses its title bar: the bookcase now starts right under the tabs, and the book count is lettered in gold on its base.
entries.detail: Ian: remove the dark Bookshelf bar above the case, put the count on the bookcase's bottom board, and bring the case right up under the line under the tabs. The tab already says Bookshelf, so the bar is gone; the case starts directly under the tab rule and so is taller on the screen; the count (for example 5 of 50 books) is lettered in gold on the wooden base. The case still grows a shelf for each new row of books. TO TEST: My Stuff, Bookshelf: no dark title bar; the top of the case sits right under the tab line; the count reads in gold on the bottom board; on a plan without the Bookshelf the invitation and See the plans still show. With a message above the case (over the limit), the message sits under the tabs and the case below it.

entries.summary: My Orders shows three orders across instead of four, with a bigger cover and the order's buttons beneath it, so each card is wider and shorter.
entries.detail: Ian: three across, the Check with the printer and Reorder buttons under the thumbnail, and the thumbnail a little bigger, about the width of a button. On My Orders the cards now sit at most three to a row (fewer on a narrow screen). An order with a cover shows it at about button width at the left, with its buttons stacked under it; the details take the rest of the card, so lines wrap far less. An order with no cover keeps its buttons under the details, as before. TO TEST: My Stuff, My Orders on a wide screen: three cards per row; each cover about 140px wide with Check with the printer, Reorder this book (and Delete on an unpaid order) stacked beneath it at the same width; the Format and Tracking lines fit on one line. Narrow the window: two, then one per row. Every button still works.

entries.summary: Order cover thumbnails now appear on My Orders; they were being drawn but not saved, so the card dropped them.
entries.detail: v3.0.989 drew each order's front cover correctly but could not record it: the app's database layer asks every new row for its id, and the new order_cover_thumbs table had none (Railway: column "id" does not exist). The failure made the card remove the picture, and the cover was drawn again on every visit. The table now has an id, added on the next boot to the table that already exists. TO TEST: open My Stuff, My Orders: each order shows its front cover at the left (the first visit draws them, a few seconds each); reload: they come straight back, and the Railway log shows no new [order-covers] cover failed lines and no fresh order-N-front uploads.

entries.summary: My Orders is now dark to match the Bookshelf: dark order cards with light gold lettering.
entries.detail: Ian: reverse the look on the order page, dark panels and light gold text instead of white panels and black text. On My Stuff, My Orders, each order card is now a dark panel with a gold edge; the book title and details are light gold, the labels a softer gold, and the Interior PDF, Cover PDF and Track shipment links gold. The "no orders yet" and loading messages match. Only My Orders changes: the admin order list, the Order & Publish tab and every other page are as they were. TO TEST: My Stuff, My Orders: dark cards, every line readable, the cover thumbnail still at the left, the links and the Check with the printer / Reorder / Delete buttons all visible and working. Settings, Orders (admin): unchanged.

entries.summary: Each order on My Orders now shows a small picture of its front cover, taken from the exact cover file that went to the printer.
entries.detail: TD-901 follow-on. Ian asked for covers on the orders like the Bookshelf has. Every order keeps the cover PDF that was sent to the printer, back cover, spine and front on one wide page; the server now draws just the front panel of it, once, the first time the order is shown, and keeps the picture for next time. It appears at the left of each order card. Nothing about the orders themselves changed: the picture is stored on its own, and if one cannot be drawn the card looks exactly as before. TO TEST: open My Stuff, My Orders: each order with a cover shows its front cover at the left (the first visit can take a few seconds per order); it is the front only, no spine or back. Reload: the pictures come straight back. An order with no cover file shows no picture and nothing else changes.

entries.summary: You can now add your own published stories from the Library to your Bookshelf, for quick access back to them.
entries.detail: TD-901. Until now Add to Bookshelf was hidden on your own stories in the Library and the server refused them. Ian: "allow someone to add their own stories from the library to their shelf. That might be how people want to do it. And then it's quick access to the library to find it." The button now appears on your own story's Library page and on your own story cards, and the story stands on the From the Library shelf like any other, opening its Library page. Like every Library book it does not count toward your 10 or 50. TO TEST: as Gold, open one of your own stories in the Library: Add to Bookshelf appears; add it. On the Library's Stories tab your own cards show + Bookshelf (or On your shelf). My Stuff, Bookshelf: it stands on the From the Library shelf and opens your story's page.

entries.summary: My Stuff's heading is one readable line, and the Bookshelf tab drops its white card: gold lettering on a dark bar, and a bookcase nearly as wide as the page with the background showing around it.
entries.detail: TD-901. Ian: the text at the top was very hard to read, a small vertical scroll bar sat beside the tabs, and the Bookshelf should be dark with gold lettering and the shelf as large as the page allows. My Stuff's title and description are now one line in gold and cream on a dark strip, with the tabs close beneath it. The stray scroll bar beside the tabs is gone. On the Bookshelf tab the white card is gone: Bookshelf and the book count sit in gold on a dark bar, the bookcase fills nearly the whole width, and the page background shows around it. My Orders and Published Stories are unchanged for now. TO TEST: open My Stuff: the heading reads clearly on one line (it wraps on a phone), no scroll bar beside the tabs. Bookshelf tab: gold Bookshelf and count on a dark bar, the case nearly full width, no white panel behind it. An account with an empty shelf or on Silver: the message reads clearly on its dark strip. My Orders and Published Stories look as they did.

entries.summary: The Bookshelf is bigger, the facing books show their real printed cover, Library books have their own bottom shelf, and a book you click opens on top of the shelf as an open book.
entries.detail: TD-901. Ian's notes on the first bookcase. The book count now sits on the Bookshelf title line, and the case is wider with taller shelves, so the books stand nearly to the top of each shelf. A campaign's facing book now shows the book's actual first page, the cover exactly as printed with its title, drawn once from the saved book the first time it is shown (the campaign picture shows while that is not available). Library books stand on their own shelf at the bottom, and a different one of them may face out each time you open the tab. Clicking any book opens it on top of the bookcase as an open book: its cover on the left page, its details and View, Download, Bring back to Publish and Remove on the right. Close it with the X, by clicking outside it, or with Escape. TO TEST: open My Stuff, Bookshelf. The count is on the title line. The facing books show their printed covers with titles (the first time can take a few seconds per book). Library books are on the bottom shelf; reopen the tab a few times and the facing one changes when there are several. Click a cover and a spine: the open book appears over the shelf; every button works; Remove asks first, over the open book; Bring back closes it and opens the campaign. On a phone the open book stacks the cover above the details.

entries.summary: The Bookshelf is now one dark walnut bookcase: campaigns share the shelves, each campaign's first book faces out showing its cover, and the rest of that campaign's books stand beside it as leather spines.
entries.detail: TD-901. Ian asked for the look of a panelled library bookcase, darker wood, and for campaigns to share shelves with the first book of each series facing out. My Stuff, Bookshelf is now a single walnut case with a moulded top, side posts, a base, a dark panelled back and thick shelf boards; there are always at least two shelves, and more appear as books are added. Each campaign's books stand together, oldest shelved first: the first faces out with its cover and a brass plate on the shelf naming the campaign, the rest stand as spines in that campaign's leather colour with gilt bands and title, taller and thicker for longer books. Library books stand at the end with a red ribbon. Clicking any book lifts it and opens its card below, as before. TO TEST: with books from two campaigns and a Library book, open My Stuff, Bookshelf: one bookcase; each campaign's first book shows its cover and a brass name plate; its other books are spines of one colour; the Library book is last with a ribbon. Add enough books to fill a shelf: they wrap onto the next shelf and sit on its board. Narrow the window: still a bookcase, books wrap. Click a cover and a spine: each lifts and opens its card.

entries.summary: Save to Bookshelf now appears after optimizing any version you can open, not only your own, and a shelved book now shows its version's own cover.
entries.detail: TD-901. Ian optimized someone else's version and the book saved, but no Save to Bookshelf button appeared: the button followed Go to Publish, which is hidden on a version you cannot publish. It now appears whenever a finished optimized book is saved, on any version you can open; Go to Publish and Download PDF are unchanged. Optimizing someone else's version saves the book as your own copy, so shelving it copies only your file, and Bring back puts it back as your copy of that version without touching the owner's settings. If the owner has since switched that version between Picture Book and Magazine, Bring back says so and the book stays on the shelf to view and download. Separately, shelved books took the campaign's picture as their cover, so two versions with different covers looked the same; a book now takes its version's own front cover (books shelved before this keep the cover they were saved with). TO TEST: as Tamika, open another member's version of Lily's First Day of School, Optimize, let it save: Save to Bookshelf appears (Go to Publish does not); save it. Save your own version too. My Stuff, Bookshelf: two spines with their own covers. Bring back the other member's one: it opens on their version and loads.

entries.summary: Add to Bookshelf now appears on the story cards in the Library too, not only on a story's own page.
entries.detail: TD-901. On the Library's Stories tab, a signed-in Gold or Platinum reader sees a small + Bookshelf button in the top corner of each story card that is not their own. Clicking it adds the story to the From the Library shelf on My Stuff without opening the story; the button then reads On your shelf. Stories already on your shelf show On your shelf when the page loads. The Library asks about a whole page of cards at once. TO TEST: signed in as Gold, open the Library, Stories tab: + Bookshelf on other people's cards, none on your own. Click one: it turns to On your shelf and the story does not open; clicking the rest of the card still opens the story. Scroll so more stories load: the new cards get the button too. My Stuff, Bookshelf: the story stands on From the Library. Reload the Library: that card shows On your shelf. As Silver, or signed out: no buttons.

entries.summary: The Bookshelf gets its shelves: your books stand on a wooden shelf per campaign, Bring back to Publish opens one on its Optimize tab ready to edit, order or publish, and you can add other people's books from the Library.
entries.detail: TD-901, Bookshelf release 3 of 3. My Stuff, Bookshelf now draws one wooden shelf per campaign with your books standing on it as spines (taller and thicker for longer books, the campaign cover on the spine). Click a spine for its card: View, Download, Bring back to Publish and Remove. Bring back makes that book the saved book of the version it came from again, then opens the campaign on the Optimize tab on that version and loads it, so it can be edited, ordered or published. Your layout settings are left as they are, and the Optimize tab says if they differ from the book's; only when the book was made in the other layout (Picture Book or Magazine) are they switched to the book's, because the saved book is kept under its layout. If the version already holds an optimized book that is not on your Bookshelf, it asks first: Shelve it first, Replace it, or Cancel. On a story's Library page, a signed-in Gold or Platinum reader who is not the author sees Add to Bookshelf; those stand on a From the Library shelf, open their Library page, and do not count toward your 10 or 50. TO TEST: as a Gold account with two shelved books from one campaign, open My Stuff, Bookshelf: one shelf, two spines; click one: its card. Optimize that book again and save WITHOUT shelving, then Bring back the shelved one: the Shelve it first / Replace it / Cancel choice appears. Shelve it first: a third spine appears and the old book opens on the Optimize tab on the right version; press Edit and change something (it is editable). Try Replace it on another pass: no new spine. Go to Order & Publish: the Printing line shows the book's original optimize date. Change a border setting, then Bring back: the book loads and the settings-changed note names the border; the setting is unchanged. Switch the layout to Magazine, then Bring back a Picture Book book: the message says the layout settings were switched, and Layout shows Picture Book. On someone else's Library story page, Add to Bookshelf, then My Stuff: it stands on From the Library and opens the story page; on your own story's page the button does not appear; signed out it does not appear. As Silver: no Add to Bookshelf on Library pages.

entries.summary: Save to Bookshelf: keep a finished, optimized book on your Bookshelf (Gold 10 books, Platinum 50), and view, download or remove it from My Stuff.
entries.detail: TD-901, Bookshelf release 2 of 3. On a book's Optimize tab, beside Go to Publish and Download PDF, Save to Bookshelf keeps a copy of the saved optimized book together with its layout, so it can be brought back and edited in the next update. It shows exactly when Go to Publish shows. The Bookshelf tab on My Stuff now lists your books by campaign, with View, Download and Remove, and counts them against your plan: Gold 10, Platinum 50. Silver, Copper and the Free Trial get the upgrade note. After a downgrade nothing is deleted: you can still view, download and remove, but not add. Only you see your shelf. TO TEST: as a Gold account, optimize and save a book, press Save to Bookshelf: Saved (1 of 10). Press it again: already on your Bookshelf. My Stuff, Bookshelf: the book under its campaign; View opens it, Download downloads it. Optimize the same book again and save: the shelf copy still opens (it is a copy, not the same file). Remove it: gone, count back to 0. As Silver: the button shows the upgrade note. As a player looking at someone else's version: no Save to Bookshelf button. The 10-book limit is checked by the build's own tests; filling a shelf to 10 is optional (the 11th is refused with the reason).

entries.summary: My Orders is now My Stuff: your print orders, a new Bookshelf, and your published stories, each on its own tab.
entries.detail: TD-901, Bookshelf release 1 of 3. The My Orders menu item is now My Stuff, a page with three tabs. My Orders is the orders screen exactly as it was. Published Stories is the list that used to sit at the bottom of My Account, moved here, and the links that pointed to it (the Publish to Library card and the publish dialog) now say My Stuff. Bookshelf is new: on Gold and Platinum it shows how many books your shelf holds (10 and 50) and is empty for now, because saving to it arrives in the next update; on Silver, Copper and the Free Trial it explains the Bookshelf and offers See the plans. TO TEST: open the menu, choose My Stuff; My Orders shows your orders as before. Click Bookshelf as a Gold or Platinum account (0 of 10 or 0 of 50) and as a Silver or Copper account (the upgrade note, and See the plans lands on the plans). Click Published Stories: your published books, with Remove still working. On a book's Order & Publish tab, the link under Publish to Library opens My Stuff on Published Stories. My Account no longer shows the published stories list. Back returns to where you came from.

entries.summary: Switching versions no longer leaves the previous version’s saved-book lines on screen, and a version you cannot publish no longer offers Go to Publish.
entries.detail: TD-900. Switching to a version with no saved layout left “Printing the version you saved at…” and “Publishing: … optimized, with covers” from the version you had just left, beside the correct “There is no saved layout” message. Both now go with the version. And when the version on screen is one you cannot publish, the Publishing line and the Go to Publish button (with Download PDF beside it) are hidden — the note telling you to switch back to your own version is all that shows. TO TEST: as Tamika on Lily’s First Day of School, Order & Publish, switch the version selector to Story Master — Canonical: only the no-saved-layout line, no Printing line, no Publishing line; on the Optimize tab no Go to Publish or Download PDF button. Switch back to your own version: all of them return, with the right date. Repeat three times.

entries.summary: The Order name no longer follows you to a different book.
entries.detail: TD-899. An Order name typed on one campaign’s Order & Publish tab stayed in the box after opening another campaign, and would have been saved with whichever book was actually bought. It is now cleared whenever the Order tab opens on a different book — another campaign, or another version of the same one. Your Ship to details are kept on purpose, so you do not have to retype your address. A reorder still fills in the name of the order it repeats. TO TEST: as Erin, type an Order name and a Ship to on Lily’s First Day of School and Get price; open The Lamplight Census → Publish → Order & Publish: Order name empty, Ship to still filled. Go back to Lily: still empty (it was left behind, not kept). Type a name, switch versions within one campaign: cleared. Type a name, go to another tab and come back to Order on the same book: kept. Reorder a past book from My Orders: its name is filled in.

entries.summary: The Order tab finds your saved layout straight away, and prices the book you will actually receive.
entries.detail: TD-895. After a fresh page load the Order & Publish tab could say “There is no saved layout for this book in this style” and quote the price of the unoptimized book, until Load Last Optimized File was pressed. It was asking before the page knew which version was on screen and which layout settings it had, and never asked again once it did. It now waits for both — showing “Checking for your saved layout…” for a moment — and asks again whenever either arrives. If the server ever does answer “no saved layout”, the Railway log now carries a [print-interior] no saved layout line naming the version, the layout style it looked in and the saved layouts that do exist. TO TEST: as Tamika, hard refresh, open Lily’s First Day of School → Publish, and go straight to Order & Publish WITHOUT pressing Load. Expected: a brief “Checking for your saved layout…”, then “Printing the version you saved at 9/22/2026, 9:04:07 AM”, 15 pages, and the $16.26 quote. Try it fast (before the version finishes loading) and slow. Then switch versions and back: the Order tab should follow the version.

entries.summary: “Your Layout Settings have changed” now appears only when they have — and says which one.
entries.detail: TD-897. Loading a saved optimized book could warn that the Layout Settings had changed when nobody had touched them. The saved settings and the current ones were compared as text, so the same settings written in a different order, or an older save that did not list a few internal defaults, counted as a change. They are now compared setting by setting, and only the settings you can actually change count. When something really did change the message names it, for example “Picture border: keyline to frame”. TO TEST: Load Last Optimized File on a book whose Layout you have not touched — no warning. Then change the picture border on the Layout panel and load again — the warning appears and names the border.

entries.summary: The layout list no longer flashes Comic and Gazette while the page loads.
entries.detail: TD-896. Both are withheld from customers, but the page shipped all four and removed two once the server replied, so a fast click showed them briefly. They now ship hidden and are revealed only where they are enabled for testing. TO TEST: hard refresh and open Order & Publish as fast as possible, then read Panel arrangement — only Picture Book and Magazine, at every moment.

entries.summary: Before you pay for a printed book, the printer now checks your files.
entries.detail: TD-602. When you press Prepare Your Order, the print service is now asked to check the interior file as soon as it is built, and the cover file as soon as that is built — two separate checks. The note under the button says what is happening: “Confirming your interior with the printer…”, then “Confirming your cover with the printer…”, counting up in seconds, then “Getting your price…”. IF THE PRINTER SAYS A FILE CANNOT BE PRINTED, the order stops there, before the price and before any payment, and the note shows the printer’s own explanation. IF THE PRINTER DOES NOT ANSWER (about 90 seconds for the interior, 60 for the cover), the order carries on exactly as it did before this release — the printer still checks the files when the order reaches it. Every check is written to the server log as a [file-check] line with the printer’s raw answer. TO TEST on staging: Prepare an order for a normal book and watch the note — both confirming lines should appear and the price should arrive as usual. Then read the [file-check] lines in the Railway log: each should say start, then result ok. If a line says unknown, copy it into the thread — that is the printer’s answer arriving in a shape this code did not expect, and it is the thing to fix next.

entries.summary: The help assistant no longer offers layouts that are not available.
entries.detail: It listed Comic and Gazette among the book layouts in two answers. Both are withheld from customers, so it now says Picture Book or Magazine. TO TEST: ask the help assistant how to change the book’s layout — the answer should name Picture Book and Magazine only.

entries.summary: A refused address now tells you what the printer said about it.
entries.detail: The last release promised to name the part of your address the print service objected to, and it never did — we were reading the wrong shape of answer, so every refusal fell back to the general advice. It now reads the real one, and passes on the print service’s own explanation: which field, and what is wrong with it — for example, that a postal code does not match the city and state, and what range it should be in.

entries.summary: The refusal message no longer starts mid-sentence.
entries.detail: Removing a sentence that said nothing left the message opening with "Nothing has been charged", which never said a refusal had happened. It now says the printer would not accept the order, and — when the print service did not say which part — that too.

entries.summary: A phone number is now asked for before a price, because the printer requires one.
entries.detail: The print service will not accept an address without a phone number, and nothing on the page asked for one — so a form that looked complete was refused, and the refusal did not say why. The page and the server now both ask for it, on every address, whatever the country.

entries.summary: One list decides what a shipping address needs.
entries.detail: The page was checking some of the required fields and the server was checking others, which is how a field neither of them knew about reached the printer. There is now a single list, and the page simply follows it.

entries.summary: When the printer refuses an address, it says which part it refused.
entries.detail: The old message said the request had been refused and left you to work out what was wrong. The print service usually names the field it objected to, so where it does, we now say so — the phone number, the postal code, the city. Where it does not, you get the general advice as before, and nothing has been charged either way.

entries.summary: A price that fails because of your address now says so, instead of blaming the book format.
entries.detail: If the printer refused a quote, we were telling you the binding, paper and colour did not work for a book that length — and asking you to try other formats. An incomplete address produced exactly that message, so there was no format to find. The printer now has to name the product code before we describe it as a format problem; everything else says to check the shipping address.

entries.summary: The price check asks for a missing name, street or city before it asks the printer.
entries.detail: Country, state and postcode were already checked on the page. Name, street and city were not, so a half-filled form went to the print service to be refused. It now says which line is missing.

entries.summary: "Run Optimize first" no longer appears on a book that has a saved layout.
entries.detail: On the Order & Publish screen the Publishing line could say nothing was ready while the line beneath it named the layout you saved and the time you saved it. The first was going by whether you had opened the Optimize screen in this browser session; it now asks the server, like its neighbour does.

entries.summary: The version in the page footer is the version you are running.
entries.detail: It has read v3.0.0 since it was first typed there, which is the number a confused reader would quote to us. It now comes from the running build.

entries.summary: Escape now backs out of the "replace your Summary?" question instead of starting the run.
entries.detail: The question about replacing a Summary you had edited by hand offered two answers and both of them started writing. Pressing Escape -- which is how most people back out of a button they did not mean to press -- counted as "keep mine" and generated anyway. It now offers three: Don’t generate, Keep mine, Replace it. Escape and a click outside the box both mean Don’t generate.

entries.summary: Cancelling a narrative no longer leaves the button stuck reading "Writing narrative...".
entries.detail: After a cancel, the Generate Narrative button kept its busy label on every session in the campaign until the page was reloaded, which read as "still working" when nothing was running. The button now returns to its normal label the moment a run is cancelled, wherever you are.

entries.summary: A narrative cancelled in its first moments really is cancelled.
entries.detail: There was a short window at the start of a run -- after the Cancel button appeared, before the run had been registered -- where pressing Cancel stopped the progress bar but never reached the server. The narrative finished writing minutes later, replaced the prose that was there, and spent the tokens. A cancel in that window is now held and delivered as soon as there is something to deliver it to, so nothing is written and nothing is charged.

entries.summary: The empty Summary box named the wrong button.
entries.detail: The grey prompt inside an empty Summary For Next Session credited the wrong button, while the line directly above it, in the same box, named the right one. Both now say Generate Narrative.

entries.summary: Summary For Next Session is now written as bullets, and stops filling the space.
entries.detail: The memory was reaching its limit after two sessions and paying for it in the wrong places — an exact count became "higher than the tally", and a detail that mattered dropped out. The fault was not the size of the box: it was being asked for a summary of a certain length, so it wrote one. It is now asked for short bullet lines of only what the next session cannot work out for itself — running counts with their actual figures, what has been established, what is promised or owed, what is still open, and who has what. The cast is no longer listed, because the character list is already sent with every run. Numbers are never blurred into comparisons; if something has to go, a whole line goes instead. The character limit is unchanged and is now a ceiling rather than a target.

entries.summary: Players in a paying Story Master’s campaign can order prints and publish again — the buttons were refusing them for a watermark their book does not have.
entries.detail: Found by the test bots. A Free Trial player in a campaign run by a Story Master on a paid plan gets a clean book — no watermark on the storyboard, the preview, the cover, the interior or the credits — and the server was perfectly willing to print it. The ORDER BUTTON refused anyway, greyed out, with a message about Free Trial books being watermarked. It was asking the wrong question: are YOU on a free trial, rather than is THIS BOOK watermarked. The two are different the moment you are playing in somebody else’s campaign. THE SAME WRONG QUESTION GUARDED PUBLISHING, one click later — which is why Publish to Library looked available and would have turned you away. Both now ask the server, which answers with exactly the test it enforces with, so the button you see and the decision you get can no longer disagree. NOTHING IS LOOSENED FOR ANYONE ELSE: your own book on a Free Trial is still watermarked and still cannot be printed, and the server still has the final say on every order and every publish. If it cannot tell, the button stays live and the server gives you an honest reason rather than the browser inventing one. TO TEST: as a Free Trial member of a campaign whose Story Master is on a paid plan, order a print and publish to the library — both should go through. Then in your OWN campaign on a Free Trial, both should still refuse.

entries.summary: The Summary box now fills in as soon as a narrative run finishes, its heading is readable again, and the help bot knows how the whole thing works.
entries.detail: Three things found by using v3.0.969 rather than by reading it. THE BOX DID NOT UPDATE UNTIL YOU RELOADED THE PAGE. The Summary was being written correctly — the box simply never re-read it, because it only refreshed when you ENTERED the Storyboard tab, and you are already there when you press the button. It now refreshes whenever any generation finishes, including a single panel Regen. THE HEADING WAS GREY ON BROWN. It is back to the same bold gold as the panel titles beside it. WE HAD BEEN NAMING THE WRONG BUTTON. Several notes and the panel itself credited the wrong one. It does not — Generate Story builds the panels from your transcript; GENERATE NARRATIVE writes the prose and the Summary. Every one of those lines is corrected, including in the earlier release notes, because a wrong instruction people are reading is worse than an edited record. AND THE HELP BOT NOW KNOWS THE FEATURE — ask it what the Summary For Next Session box is, how to stop a session inheriting the last one, or whose memory gets used, and it can answer. TO TEST: run Generate Narrative and watch the box fill without touching the page; check the heading reads as gold, not grey; and ask the help bot about the Summary For Next Session.

entries.summary: Your story now remembers itself — when you Generate Narrative, the previous session’s Summary is carried forward into the new one.
entries.detail: v3.0.967 gave every session a Summary For Next Session. This is the half that reads it back. WHEN YOU GENERATE A NARRATIVE, the previous session’s Summary is handed to the writer as established fact — placed after your campaign’s Lore and before this session’s panels, so it bridges the world you set up and the scene being written now. The prose can lean on who these people are to each other and what was left hanging, without retelling it. AND IT KEEPS ROLLING. The new Summary does not start from scratch: it begins from the one carried forward, keeps what still matters, adds what this session changed, and drops what is now settled — one running memory of the whole campaign rather than a stack of session recaps. It is told to drop what matters LEAST rather than what is OLDEST, so a fact established in session three can still be there in session forty. WHICH SESSION, AND WHOSE: the box now tells you what it is carrying and where it came from. Each version keeps its own memory, so it uses yours if you have one for the previous session, and the Story Master’s if you do not — which is what happens for anyone who joined partway through. NOTHING BREAKS WHEN THERE IS NOTHING TO CARRY. The first session of a campaign, or one whose predecessor has no Summary yet, simply writes its own and says so. TO TEST: generate session one, read its Summary, then generate session two — the prose should be aware of session one without retelling it, and session two’s Summary should CARRY FORWARD what still matters rather than describing only itself. Then edit session one’s Summary by hand, regenerate session two, and confirm your edit is what got used.

entries.summary: The Summary For Next Session box now saves on its own — the Save button is gone.
entries.detail: It works the way the campaign Lore and Story Instructions boxes already do: your typing is written a moment after you stop, and clicking away writes it immediately rather than waiting. A short Saving then Saved appears beside the box so you can see it happen. NOTHING IS WRITTEN UNLESS YOU ACTUALLY CHANGED SOMETHING — clicking into the box to read it and clicking out again does nothing at all, which matters because editing the Summary is what makes Generate Narrative ask before replacing it. Only one save is ever in the air at once; if you keep typing while one is being written, the next one goes out when it returns, so two saves can never land out of order and overwrite the newer text with the older. If a save fails the message stays on screen and says so rather than disappearing — an autosave that fails quietly is worse than a button, because nobody clicked anything and nobody is watching. TO TEST: type in the box, wait a moment, and watch Saved appear; switch tabs and come back to confirm it stuck. Then click into the box, change nothing, click away — nothing should save, and Generate Narrative should NOT ask you about replacing it.

entries.summary: A new Summary For Next Session box at the bottom of the Storyboard — a short, editable memory of what happened, written for you when you Generate Narrative.
entries.detail: Each session now keeps a short note of what happened in it, written for the NEXT session to read: who matters now, where they are, what they are trying to do, and what is still unresolved. It sits at the very bottom of the Storyboard tab and you can edit every word of it. IT COSTS NOTHING EXTRA. Generate Narrative already asks the model for a handful of short summaries while it writes the prose, and this is one more field in the same answer — no second run and no extra tokens. THE LENGTH IS CAPPED AND THE MODEL KNOWS THE CAP BEFORE IT WRITES, so it keeps what still matters and lets go of what does not, rather than a fifty-session campaign ending up with a wall of text. The limit is set on the Dashboard and starts at 1,500 characters. YOURS IS KEPT: once you have edited the Summary, generating the narrative again asks before replacing it, and saying keep mine changes nothing else about the run. Leaving it blank is perfectly fine and breaks nothing. Each version has its own, like every other per-version setting — you can read another version Summary but not write it. WHAT IS NOT HERE YET: nothing reads the Summary back. Feeding it to the next session, so the story remembers itself, is the next release. TO TEST: open a session with a storyboard, run Generate Narrative, and read what appears in the box at the bottom. (Generate Story builds the panels from the transcript; Generate Narrative writes the prose and the Summary.) Edit it, save, switch tabs and come back to confirm it stuck. Then run Generate Narrative again and check you are asked before it is replaced.

entries.summary: A renewal receipt now shows the tokens that expired, so the balance on your account and the number on the receipt add up.
entries.detail: TD-841, from a tester who could not make the two agree and was right not to be able to. Your monthly grant expires whatever use-it-or-lose-it tokens are left over and THEN grants the new period, so your balance moves by the grant minus the expiry — while the receipt quoted only the grant. 442 minus 2 expired plus 30 granted is 470, the receipt said 30, and both numbers were correct; nothing on the screen or in the email named the 2. The receipt now carries an Expired from last period line between Tokens added and Token balance, so the three read as arithmetic. TOKENS ADDED STILL MEANS THE GRANT and deliberately so — it is what your plan buys and what the charge is for; a net figure would be right for the header and wrong for an invoice. The line appears only when something actually expired, so a first subscription and an upgrade look exactly as they did. TO TEST: renew on an account holding leftover use-it-or-lose-it tokens and check the three numbers on the receipt reconcile against the header.

entries.summary: Upgrading your plan mid-month now sends an email explaining the tokens that just arrived and when the charge lands.
entries.detail: TD-842. An upgrade grants the difference in monthly tokens the moment it takes effect, but Stripe prorates the CHARGE onto your next invoice — so no payment happened that day, so the receipt every purchase gets (v3.0.961) never ran, and tokens simply appeared with nothing to explain them. Weeks later a proration receipt arrived for a plan change you had been using ever since. The upgrade now sends its own email when it happens, naming the new plan, the tokens added, and the fact that there is nothing to pay today because the charge follows on the next invoice. It cannot send twice on a Stripe retry, and it can never delay or block the tokens themselves. The v3.0.961 release note has also been corrected — it said the charge was taken immediately, which it is not (TD-843). TO TEST: upgrade a subscription mid-cycle and check one email arrives naming the new plan and the tokens, with no amount on it; then confirm the later proration receipt still arrives with the next invoice.

entries.summary: Renaming a campaign now carries the change onto the book, when the book title was never chosen by hand.
entries.detail: Reported from the tester list. A book whose title you have never typed is seeded with the campaign name so that something is always on the cover — and from that moment it was a stored value, so renaming the campaign left the OLD name on the book for good. A rename now carries onto any book title that is still exactly the old campaign name, which is the only case in which nobody chose it. A TITLE YOU TYPED IS NEVER TOUCHED, including one that merely resembles the campaign name. TO TEST: rename a campaign whose book title you have never edited and check the cover and the title page follow it; then set a title of your own, rename again, and check yours survives.

entries.summary: The two token tiles on My Account now say in plain words what each kind of token is.
entries.detail: TD-845. The Usage panel showed UTOLT TOKENS and CARRY-OVER TOKENS with a number under each and nothing else. UTOLT is an acronym, and an acronym on a screen is a word only the people who built it can read. Each tile now carries a small line underneath saying what it means: Use Them or Lose Them, and Yours to Keep. NOTHING ABOUT THE NUMBERS CHANGED -- this is wording. The two tiles are the whole token model in miniature and they explain each other, which is why both got a line rather than only the confusing one. WHAT THE TWO ACTUALLY MEAN, since this is the first place it has been written down for a reader: the first tile is the tokens that come with your plan each month. They refresh on your billing date and they do not roll over, so it is worth spending them first -- and the app does spend them first, before it touches the other kind. The second tile is tokens you bought, or that came with a pass, a bonus or a plan upgrade. Those are yours and they never expire. Everything you pay for outright lands in the second tile; only the plan itself and an upgrade to it put tokens in the first. TO TEST: My Account -> Usage. Both token tiles have a small line under the label, dimmer and smaller than the label itself. The numbers are unchanged, and the five tiles beside them are untouched.

entries.summary: Print orders now get a proper order number -- CMP-2026-00042 -- instead of the short internal po- tag.
entries.detail: TD-839. Every print order was labelled po- followed by its row number: po-7, po-42. That is a database id with a prefix on it, and it was what the confirmation email showed, what the printer was told, and what support had to ask a customer to read out. THE NEW NUMBER CARRIES THE YEAR AND SORTS PROPERLY: CMP-2026-00042. Five digits, so the ten-thousandth order of a year still lines up under the ones before it. The year is the year the order was placed and it is fixed at that moment -- an order placed in December still reads 2026 when you look at it in January. The digits are the order id itself, so they keep counting rather than restarting; the year says when, not how many. ORDERS PLACED BEFORE THIS KEEP THE NUMBER THEY WERE GIVEN. A number that has already gone out on a confirmation email, and that the printer already knows the job by, does not get quietly relabelled -- old orders stay po- and are still found by it. THE NUMBER IS DECIDED ONCE, WHERE THE ORDER IS CREATED, AND EVERYTHING ELSE READS IT. The printer, the confirmation email, the problem email and the support report all take the same value, so none of them can drift into naming the order something the others do not recognise. THE TWO ORDER EMAILS ALSO GOT THE TABLE FIX from v3.0.963: fixed column widths, so a long book title or a tracking number cannot push the details past the edge of the panel the way an internal key did to the purchase receipts. TO TEST: Dashboard -> Settings -> Email preview / test-send -> Print order confirmed, and Print order problem. The order number reads CMP- then a year then five digits, every label sits on one line, and nothing runs outside the panel. Then place a real order: the number on screen, the number in the email and the number the printer shows must all be the same one.

entries.summary: Purchase receipts now show a short Purchase ID instead of a long internal key, and the token pack and pass receipts no longer spill outside the panel.
entries.detail: TD-838. The token pack and Platinum Pass receipts came out broken — labels wrapping onto two lines, values shoved right, and the reference line running clean off the edge of the panel. The subscription one looked perfect. THE LAYOUT WAS THE SYMPTOM; THE FIELD WAS THE BUG. Every receipt carried a Reference, and that was the id STRIPE uses internally — not a purchase number, and no use to anybody reading it. A subscription invoice id is about 27 characters and fits; a checkout session id, which is what a pack and a pass produce, is about 55 with no space or hyphen anywhere in it. A table column cannot break a run with nothing to break on, so it grew until it fit and pushed everything else out of shape. That is why exactly two of the three were wrong, and why the third looked fine while being just as wrong in substance. NOW IT IS A PURCHASE ID, AND ONLY WHEN THERE IS ONE. A token pack and a pass each write a purchase record, so they show tp-00042 — short, ours, and the same shape as the po- numbers print orders already use. A subscription charge has no purchase record at all, so the line is simply not there rather than showing something only support could use. The detail table also has fixed column widths now, so no future value can push it around the way that id did. TO TEST: Dashboard → Settings → Email preview / test-send. Send the token pack and Platinum Pass receipts — every label on one line, every value inside the panel, and a Purchase ID line reading tp- followed by five digits. Send the subscription, renewal and plan-change ones — they should look exactly as they did before EXCEPT that the Reference line is gone.

entries.summary: The admin Email preview / test-send list now carries all five purchase receipts.
entries.detail: TD-837. v3.0.961 added a receipt for every purchase, and there was no way to look at one without spending money in the Stripe sandbox. The Dashboard’s Email preview / test-send dropdown now offers all five — token pack, Platinum Pass, subscription started, subscription renewal, and plan change — each filled with realistic sample figures and sent to your own admin address with [TEST] on the subject. THE PREVIEW IS THE REAL EMAIL, not a copy of it. The subject line and the opening sentence for each receipt kind used to be written in routes/tokens.js, right beside the code that sends it. A preview that restated them would have been a second copy, free to drift, and a preview that shows something a customer never receives is worse than no preview. Both now live in one place in routes/email.js, and the preview and the live send go through the SAME function — so what lands in your inbox is byte-for-byte what a customer gets. TO TEST: Dashboard → Settings → Email preview / test-send. Send each of the five receipt entries and check the amounts, the token counts and the pass expiry read sensibly, then confirm the subject lines match the ones on the real receipts from the previous release.

entries.summary: Every purchase now sends a receipt by email — token packs, Platinum Passes, and every subscription charge including renewals.
entries.detail: TD-836, from the tester run: a Platinum Pass was bought twice and no email arrived either time. Print orders have always sent a confirmation; NOTHING ELSE DID. A token pack, a pass and a subscription all took money and sent silence, and a monthly renewal has never sent anything at all — so a customer charged in month seven had no record of it from us. THE RECEIPT NOW COMES FROM ONE PLACE. Every purchase lands in the same Stripe webhook, and each kind of purchase hands back a description of what was bought; one block at the end sends the receipt. That matters more than it sounds: the reason three of these were missing is that each fulfilment path was written separately and nobody could see the whole set at once. Now “did this purchase send a receipt” is one function to read. WHAT IS ON IT: what you bought, what you paid, the card it went on where Stripe tells us, the tokens added and your new balance, and for a pass the tier and the date it runs to. IT CANNOT SEND TWICE. Stripe retries webhooks routinely, and a duplicate receipt for a real charge is its own support conversation. Each receipt is recorded against the Stripe session or invoice id, and a retry finds the record and sends nothing — while a retry after a MAIL failure still tries again, because those are different questions and were deliberately not merged. A receipt that fails to send is logged as an error and raises an alert rather than disappearing. RENEWALS AND UPGRADES BOTH COUNT (Ian: every charge). A monthly renewal sends a receipt. AN UPGRADE IS TWO EVENTS, AND THIS NOTE ORIGINALLY DESCRIBED ONLY THE GAP BETWEEN THEM.
